entries.title: Notice Accompanying the Provisional Map
entries.body:
The route sheet links three observations: a tag with unverified initials, a wheel trace that ends before the rebuilt section and a repeated chime pattern in the Choir. None confirms that Ellis Porter traveled between those places. The sheet is a prompt for comparison, not a claim of arrival.

The notice names each source and its limits. It records who reviewed the copy, when it was delivered and whether a measurement was later corrected. The map uses dotted lines where there is no continuous physical trace. A recipient may request a private reading or ask the keeper to remove their testimony from future copies.

One policy sends the provisional copy immediately. That gives Nella access while she decides whether to pursue it. Another waits for a measuring cycle, with a review date entered before the delay begins. Either route preserves the draft and the right to change the schedule.

The choice governs this archive's handling of uncertain evidence. It does not decide what Nella should believe or become a statement about another family. New sources will be appended with their own dates instead of being used to rewrite the old uncertainty.

entries.title: Delivered with the Gap Marked
entries.body:
I chose to see the provisional map. It places the visible wheel scrapes beside the old Lockhouse route, but the dotted section is wider than I expected. The chime timing is written in numbers, with the instrument's error beside them. No sentence claims that Ellis spoke through the bell.

The copy includes my request, the date Rowan handed it to me and the witness to the transfer. I can ask for a correction if a date or source is wrong. I cannot change a measurement merely because I hoped it would point somewhere else.

Seeing the map gives me another question to ask. It does not give me my brother back, and it does not give me a place to bury him. I may carry this copy while I keep looking, but the page must not be shown as a confirmed route in a public memorial.

The archive retains its earlier draft beside my copy. If I later find a letter, we will attach it as new evidence. Until then, the line remains dotted and the name remains a possibility I am allowed to question.

entries.title: A Review Date for the Sealed Copy
entries.body:
I asked Rowan to hold the provisional map through the next measuring cycle. The archive keeps an index showing that the map exists, the date it was completed and the person responsible for the seal. Withholding the copy does not erase the evidence.

The review date is written beside the reason for waiting. I can change my mind before that date, and I can request that an independent examiner repeat the chime measurement. If I do not return, the record says the review did not happen; it does not convert silence into consent.

The public index contains no route claim and no personal name beyond the fact that a family requested time. Two custodians must open the packet together. Each opening is logged, even if they decide to make no change. The method stays visible so a temporary seal cannot become a permanent disappearance.

I still do not know whether Ellis passed through the Lockhouse. Waiting is a choice about when I receive one uncertain map, not a verdict about my brother. The question remains open, and the date gives me a way to return to it.

entries.title: The Map Behind the Seed List
entries.body:
My great-grandmother used the back of a seed ledger to draw a set of stars. The crop order on the front is dated, but the chart has no date. A short note says that the northern point moved against the sun. There is no name for the observer and no entry showing where the paper went afterward.

Our family kept the sheet because the outer edge carries a second fold, like the mark left by a parcel envelope. No seal or address survives. For several generations we told one another that she had sent a message through the Veil. The story grew while the paper remained unchanged.

I cannot prove that she sent anything. I can prove that the page is old enough to have been used with the seed ledger and that its ink has not been replaced in the last two generations. Those are small facts, but they belong in the same account as our family's hope.

The first comparison should preserve the torn corner and the scale of the paper. If we straighten the chart or supply the missing note, we will lose the difference between what she drew and what we wish she had meant.

entries.title: A Rubbing with an Unlabeled Dot
entries.body:
The rubbing records two parallel marks, an offset dot and the remaining edge of a line that ends at a tear. There is no legend for these symbols. The dot could be a star, a pin hole or a later mark made while the ledger was stored.

We placed the paper beside a measured grid without flattening the torn corner. A small shift changes the inferred angle. For that reason the transcript records a range of possible positions rather than selecting the cleanest looking one.

The family map is useful as a historical source because we know which household kept it and which page it was drawn on. That provenance does not make its astronomical interpretation correct. It only lets another examiner see where the sheet came from.

The archive keeps the rubbing and a photograph of the original. Neither copy contains a connecting line that was not present on the paper. If a future measurement identifies one symbol, the interpretation can be dated and attached without overwriting this first reading.

entries.title: The West Root Temperature Sheet
entries.body:
The western root well has dark rings on the side facing the irrigation channel. Their spacing overlaps the dates of two late waterings and a mild frost. We did not have a thermometer at the eastern bed during those nights, so the record cannot isolate water from air temperature.

A greener ring is visible inside the area watered most often. Beyond that area, several shallow channels end before reaching the dry rows. The observations support a difference in soil conditions. They do not identify the cause as magic, root pressure or unequal watering without another controlled comparison.

I used the same ruler at both beds and wrote down the distance from each root flare. One measurement was repeated by a second gardener who did not know which row I expected to be cooler. Her reading fell inside my margin of error.

The old council ledger combines all water collected at the well into one total. This sheet keeps the beds separate. It asks which places received water on which dates, a question that may improve the next harvest even if it never explains the green boundary around our village.

entries.title: The Water Mara Measured
entries.body:
I have measured the water at the root well and along the channel. The healthy orchard is real. The soil outside the watered ring is dry enough to crack, and the seedbed has been narrowed twice since I became its keeper.

The World Will says that energy moved from other regions so Greenwake could stay fertile. I heard that explanation in the same conversation in which the Crown was offered to Rowan. I did not see the transfer, and my field ledger does not measure energy. The explanation is testimony from a powerful source, not a result written by my instruments.

My measurements show which rows received water, how many times we opened each sluice and where the channel stopped. They cannot show whether the world was saved elsewhere or how many people paid that cost. I will not turn an honest observation into proof of a larger claim.

Anyone may repeat the water measurements. We keep the dates, gauge height and blank days visible. A missing measurement is not zero water, and it is not permission to invent a number.

entries.title: Two Clocks at the Outer-Wake Mast
entries.body:
The handheld clock and the mast clock did not agree when the wind shifted. Both instruments worked, but their times had not been aligned before the first observation. A difference of several minutes changes which star position appears beside a short gust.

We repeated the reading with both clocks visible in the same frame. The wind came from the outer aperture on each pass, within the tolerance of the vane. The timing did not match closely enough to claim that one gust repeated the signal on Owen's sheet.

Wind direction describes where air moved at the mast during a measured interval. It does not identify what caused the movement or whether anyone intended it. The old report's phrase a voice from beyond has no corresponding measurement in our notebook.

A later team can synchronize the clocks, leave the instruments running through several seasons and compare the record with changes in the aperture. Until that work exists, the file carries two times and one bounded direction.

entries.title: Farwake Carp as a Local Sample
entries.body:
The Farwake Carp was caught at Celestial Pool during the same local hour as the wind reading. Its presence shows that the fish lived in the pool that day. It is a biological sample from the lake, not a courier and not a listener capable of confirming a distant transmission.

We recorded the location, hour, lure and water conditions before release. No tissue was taken. The fish showed no unusual response when the mast changed direction, though our observation window was too short to treat an absence of response as meaningful.

A local sample can help describe the environment around a measurement. A second team can compare species, water temperature and the same wind interval in another season. That would tell us whether the setting changed between readings.

It cannot tell us whether the star chart was sent, received or understood. Those are separate questions requiring separate records. The ledger files the fish beneath sampling conditions, not beneath the map's interpretation.

entries.title: The Overlay Keeps Both Angles
entries.body:
We aligned three stars that appear on both the old Greenwake rubbing and the current Outer-Wake chart. Two possible overlays remain after accounting for the torn paper edge. One places the unexplained line nearer the west aperture; the other falls within the chart's measurement error.

The overlay does not show a known transmitter. No receiver log names a sender, and no synchronized clock connects the old page to a present-day pulse. The family's memory that the line pointed toward the Veil is recorded beside the chart, not drawn over it.

The first observer may have used a different horizon or a local landmark hidden by the fold. Each possibility can be tested if we find a dated survey from the same village. Until then, the chart gives us two hypotheses and a useful place to point another telescope.

We keep both overlays because neither earns the right to replace the other. A precise-looking line would be easier to copy, but could conceal uncertainty that a later observer might otherwise resolve.

entries.title: Copy Three, with the Torn Edge
entries.body:
The third copy combines the rubbing, the clock comparison and the current star chart. It shows where the first line was visible, where the paper is torn and which observations depend on clocks that were not synchronized.

The new copy is less certain than the story I inherited. That does not make it useless. It gives me a reproducible method and a list of conditions another traveler can check. If a future signal repeats, we can record the time, weather, position and duration before discussing what it means.

I asked that my family name stay attached to the seed ledger because it explains why we preserved the paper. Rowan's field notes remain separate because he made the measurements. Mara's water account is a third source, and it does not claim that the map explains Greenwake's harvest.

The copy ends with an open space for a new observation. It is not a destination, invitation or promise of rescue. I can keep asking what my great-grandmother intended without pretending the paper already answers me.

entries.title: Open Procedure for Repeating the Chart
entries.body:
The public method lists the coordinates of each observation point, local and mast clock readings, weather, telescope scale and condition of the paper rubbing. A second observer can repeat the steps without adopting the same theory about what the stars mean.

The notice includes the Farwake Carp sample as context for the lake environment, not as evidence of communication. It explains why the sample was released and why no behavior was described as a response. Readers may ask for a new survey without changing the original map.

Every copy carries a version number. Corrections add a dated page that states what changed and who requested it. Earlier readings stay attached so a later summary cannot erase a result that contradicted its preferred interpretation.

Publishing a method makes scrutiny easier, but can make an incomplete result appear official. The notice says that no sender, receiver or destination has been identified. It invites measurements and disagreement, not belief.

entries.title: A Private Copy with a Review Date
entries.body:
Owen received copy three with a record of who made each measurement and which questions remain unresolved. The copy is available to the people who prepared or preserved the source material. They may request wider release after checking the dates and the description of the damaged paper.

A limited copy is not secret proof. The access list says who has seen it; the document makes no claim that a response came from beyond the Veil. If a recipient asks for a household detail to be removed, the archive records the change without altering the telescope readings.

The review date is written beside the reason for limiting access. At that time Owen may open the copy to all readers, keep the same group with a new date or ask for another measurement first. No one may treat a missed appointment as permanent consent.

This policy protects the people who hold the family record while the method is being checked. It preserves a path toward public review. The chart remains an unfinished observation and may be handled differently when evidence changes.

entries.title: A Column Before the Planting
entries.body:
Tờ folio còn sót lại có hai cột: lượng lương thực đã cân và lượng dự kiến sau mùa gieo. Một bản chép ở Crownfall bỏ mất dòng tiêu đề, khiến con số trong cột thứ hai trông như một phép cân thực tế. Dấu ngày cho thấy bản dự tính được lập trước khi luống bắt đầu gieo hạt.

Hai bản giấy khác nhau ở cách ghi, nhưng không chỉ ra ai đã bỏ dòng tiêu đề, vì sao họ làm vậy hay người nào đã đọc bản sau cùng. Không được gọi sự khác biệt này là bằng chứng giả mạo. Nó là bằng chứng cho thấy hồ sơ mất một nhãn quan trọng.

Ada đề nghị mọi bản chép mới phải giữ tiêu đề, ngày, phương pháp và nguồn của từng số. Nếu một trường không có chứng từ, chỗ ấy phải được đánh dấu là chưa xác minh thay vì điền bằng một ước tính khác.

entries.title: The Sliding Peg at the Granary
entries.body:
Thước đo ở kho thóc vẫn có thể trượt giữa ba lỗ neo. Dấu sơn hiện tại cho biết mức “đủ dùng trong bốn ngày”, nhưng không ghi ngày đặt, tên trạm, loại thóc hay người đặt thước. Một lỗ neo đã mòn hơn hai lỗ còn lại.

Vật này cho biết cách những người giữ kho biểu diễn một ngưỡng dự phòng. Nó không cho biết lượng thóc thực sự nằm trong từng kho, cũng không chứng minh mức dự phòng đã được gửi đến cộng đồng nào.

Nếu tiếp tục sử dụng, Ada muốn niêm phong thước sau khi chụp vị trí hiện tại và bắt đầu một phép đo mới có khối lượng, ngày, loại hạt cùng người chứng kiến. Bản cũ được giữ riêng làm vật chứng về cách ghi, không làm chuẩn sản lượng.

entries.title: A Waterline from One Afternoon
entries.body:
Vạch trên thước ven Starlit Lake được đánh sau một cơn mưa. Dòng ghi giờ đo và hướng gió bị rách, còn dấu mực chỉ liên tục trong khoảng hai gang tay. Không có chuỗi quan sát từ những ngày trước hoặc sau để xác định hồ đang dâng hay rút.

Tờ folio lại đặt cạnh vạch đó một dự tính mực nước cho cuối mùa. Việc đặt cạnh nhau có thể khiến người đọc tưởng rằng một lần đo đã xác nhận cả dự tính. Mực nước tại một vị trí vẫn là dữ liệu thật, nhưng nó không đại diện cho toàn hồ hoặc toàn mùa.

Bản khảo sát mới phải ghi vị trí, giờ địa phương, mưa gần nhất và sai số đọc vạch. Một quan sát khác nhau không làm vạch cũ biến mất; hai bản cần nằm cạnh nhau với điều kiện đo rõ ràng.

entries.title: Alden’s Distribution Signature
entries.body:
Captain Alden Vale xác nhận chữ ký dưới bảng phân phối. Ông tin dự tính sản lượng dựa trên một chu kỳ trước và chuyển thóc khỏi một số thung lũng để duy trì trạm đèo. Ông không có sổ cân gốc, và thừa nhận đã ký khi tiêu đề đo lường không còn nguyên.

Lời xác nhận chứng minh Alden đã ký và mô tả điều ông tin lúc đó. Nó không xác định ai đã đổi dòng tiêu đề, bao nhiêu lương thực thật đã chuyển, hoặc một cách phân phối khác sẽ cứu được bao nhiêu người.

Bản ghi giữ chữ ký cùng lời giới hạn của người ký. Xóa chữ ký sẽ che khuất trách nhiệm; biến nó thành chứng cứ cho mọi quyết định phía trước sẽ nói quá điều người này có thể biết.

entries.title: One Emberroot Bed Is One Sample
entries.body:
Một luống Emberroot được gieo dưới lớp tro mỏng ở Crownfall Reach. Ghi chép mới lưu số hạt gieo, số mầm sống, lượng nước, ngày chăm và ngày thu hoạch. Kết quả cho thấy rễ có thể mọc tại đúng luống này trong điều kiện hiện tại.

Đây là mẫu thực địa đầu tiên của lượt khảo sát, không phải mức năng suất trung bình, kết quả của mọi nông trại hay bảo đảm cho mùa kế tiếp. Các luống không được đo vẫn còn là chỗ trống trong sổ.

Ada giữ hạt còn lại cho một lượt lặp với người làm vườn ở vùng khác. Lượt sau cần cùng cách đếm nhưng không được giả định đất, lượng mưa hoặc người chăm giống hệt nhau.

entries.title: One Minnow at the Shore
entries.body:
Một Starlit Minnow được câu ở bờ phía tây vào buổi chiều có ghi trên biên nhận. Mẫu xác nhận rằng ít nhất một cá thể còn sống trong hồ tại thời điểm đó. Nó không trả lời số lượng cá, độ sâu của đàn, tỉ lệ sống hay việc những hồ khác còn cá hay không.

Dấu nhịp trên vảy không được dùng để kết luận có người hay sinh vật nào gửi tín hiệu từ ngoài Veil. Ada ghi loài, vị trí, thời tiết và công cụ câu để nhóm sau có thể tìm hiểu sinh thái, nhưng giữ riêng giả thuyết về nguồn phát.

Một con cá không thể đại diện cho hồ. Tuy vậy, nếu hồ có thể nuôi được sự sống, các phép đo tương lai phải quan sát nó thay vì coi nó là một con số phụ trong bảng dự báo.

entries.title: Expected Is Not Observed
entries.body:
Bản lệnh của The World Will mô tả những giá trị mong đợi theo một biên độ thay đổi. Nó nói rõ mô hình được tính từ chu kỳ từng được quan sát, nhưng không lưu từng bao thóc, buổi gieo hay kho cụ thể tạo nên đầu vào.

Một mô hình có thể lặp lại đúng phép tính với cùng giả định. Điều đó không biến giả định thành vật đã được đếm. Trang này không chứng minh rằng World Will cố tình che số; nó cho thấy hồ sơ của mô hình và hồ sơ kiểm kê là hai loại chứng cứ khác nhau.

Khi trình bày kết quả, phải nêu giả định đầu vào, khoảng sai số và phần dữ liệu bị thiếu. Người đọc có thể cân nhắc mức rủi ro, nhưng không nên thay lời hứa của một người bằng lời tiên tri của một bảng tính.

entries.title: The Gatekeeper and the Missing Ledgers
entries.body:
Ta được giao giữ lối vào kho và lời thề, không phải đứng trong từng kho lương của các vùng. Qua nhiều lần sửa, có những bảng ta chỉ biết bằng bản chép lại. Ta nhớ người giữ kho cần một con số gọn để chia việc; ta không thể nhớ thay từng gia đình đã nhận gì.

Có bản chép gọi một dự tính là số đã có. Ta không biết người đầu tiên đổi tiêu đề muốn sửa lỗi, rút gọn hay làm điều gì khác. Không có tên người sửa hoặc ngày đổi, ký ức của ta không thể cung cấp chúng.

Ta ghi điều mình thấy, tách khỏi điều người khác kể và điều ta không biết. Lời khai này cũng chỉ có phạm vi như vậy: nó không xóa trách nhiệm, và không điền được những trang đã mất.

entries.title: A Public Table with Its Limits
entries.body:
Bản công khai chứa dải sai số, điều kiện đo, nguồn của từng dòng và ngày thực hiện. Tên hộ gia đình, người cân thóc và người giữ chìa khóa được giữ trong sổ riêng theo quyền của họ. Những ô không có nguồn vẫn để trống.

Trang này không chỉ ra ai phải nhận khẩu phần, không đoán được sản lượng cả mùa và không quyết định có nên tiếp tục chu kỳ. Nó cho phép người đọc xem phương pháp, lặp lại một phép đo mới và chỉ rõ khi họ suy luận xa hơn dữ liệu.

Nếu xuất hiện chứng cứ mới, người ghi phải thêm một phiên bản có ngày, không sửa bản cũ để biến nó thành dự báo đúng từ trước. Việc công khai phương pháp không đồng nghĩa công khai danh tính hoặc coi kết quả là mệnh lệnh.

entries.title: A Review Date Is Not Consent
entries.body:
Bản có tên người đo được niêm lại. Bên ngoài có biên nhận ghi nhóm được xem, ngày gửi, giới hạn của bản sao và thời điểm phải liên lạc lần nữa. Chưa có bằng chứng rằng tất cả người nhận đã đọc hoặc trả lời.

Quá hạn chỉ kích hoạt bước hỏi lại. Nó không mở hộp tự động, không chuyển sự im lặng thành đồng ý và không biến bản có tên thành tài liệu chung. Nếu cần thêm thời gian, người phụ trách phải gia hạn có ghi nhận; nếu một người yêu cầu sửa định danh, số đo gốc vẫn được giữ cạnh thay đổi.

Việc niêm phong bảo vệ quyền xem của những người có tên trong bản. Nó không khiến dữ liệu đo được biến mất; một bản tổng hợp đã lược thông tin có thể được đánh giá riêng nếu các điều kiện công khai cho phép.

entries.title: Cinderwell: A Salt Mark Is Not a Cause
entries.body:
Talia Mercer began the second Cinderwell field record after Oren Bell found two seed sacks with the same warehouse mark and different germination histories. The outer cloth on one sack had a split seam. Salt crystals were caught in the fold, but the storage wall had also been damp. The date on its wax strip documented packing; it did not document every place the sack had travelled or every time it had been wet. Rowan copied the split, the crystals and the date as separate observations.

Sister June kept three nursery trays on the same rack. Staff moved them to avoid midday sun, so their placement changed during the trial. One tray was watered after the first bell, another after the second. The germination card showed different results, but it could not isolate the effect of soil, shade, watering interval or seed batch. A corner of the card had blurred. The team left the day unread rather than choosing a convenient number.

A pale line of salt ran along a low bed and stopped at a raised stone. A weaker line appeared beyond it. Valve hours, household watering notes and visible marks used different clocks and measures. The water records did not show how long liquid remained in the furrow. A wet mark appeared after the sluice closed, but it might have been retained water, a delayed seep or moisture already held in the ground. One observation could not distinguish them.

At Dawnkeep, Rowan caught a Blackreed Trout as a source comparison. The catch record supplied a time and lake location, not the route the fish or water had travelled through. Talia would not place the trout beside a Cinderwell water value without a route log connecting the two. Instead, the team used it as a clearly labeled upstream sample, one comparison among several. The distinction prevents an attractive story about a single channel from replacing missing measurements.

The Salt Saffron wick changed shade in three samples: pale at Dawnkeep, darker in a furrow sample, and between those readings at the base of the nursery bed. On repetition, matching wicks did not always look identical. Light, drying time, trapped droplets and dye affected the comparison. The wick could sort samples into rough visual groups. It could not provide a laboratory concentration, show where salt entered, or identify who moved a valve. The notebook retained the spread between repeated readings and named the instrument's limits on its front page.

A second crop yielded more germinated seeds than the first, but it was watered on a steadier schedule. Since schedule and planting batch changed together, the difference could not be attributed to the salt line. The record kept both the higher count and timing difference. Oren also found that warehouse forms were sometimes copied at the end of a shift. A written date could refer to copying rather than weighing. The revised form has separate spaces for packing, sowing, weighing and transcription. Blank space is preferable to treating one time as another.

The available land could not support an unlimited experiment. The group discussed a paired outdoor trial: split one lot on the same sowing day, keep one bed as it is, and shield the other from the seep. That could compare the beds in one season, but it would use field soil during a shortage. The other proposal repeated two sheltered trays, swapped their positions and logged temperature. It preserved more outdoor ground and improved control over heat, while leaving the field salt edge untested. Neither plan was called the correct answer. The chosen route and its remaining question were written at the top of the next page.

Whatever design follows, the trial card stays beside the ration ledger rather than inside it. Germination counts do not establish who received water, how much was delivered, or whether any household should lose an allocation. The team recorded dates, crop, sample origin, temperature, observed colour and watering times it could verify. It left cause, responsibility and the missing travel interval open. This record describes a method and its limits; it does not prove that salt alone damaged the seed.

entries.title: Cinderwell: Two Beds, One Missed Hour
entries.body:
The paired outdoor trial divided a single marked seed lot between two beds. Both were sown during the same morning. One bed kept its ordinary exposure to the furrow; a temporary screen was placed between the other bed and a narrow seep mark. The purpose was limited: observe whether the two beds produced different germination counts under the recorded conditions. It was not a test of which household should receive water or which worker had opened a valve.

The sowing was recorded on one card and watering times on another. On the second day the screened bed received water later than the ordinary bed. The worker had been sent to help move a nursery rack, and the route between beds was obstructed by a repaired channel. The missed hour was not hidden. It remained in the table as a difference between conditions. The paired comparison was imperfect, even though the original seed lot, sowing day and bed preparation had been documented.

The ordinary bed showed a higher germination count when Rowan inspected both rows. That count is an observation. It does not show that the salt line reduced germination in the screened bed: the later watering, uneven shade, drainage around the screen or random variation in a small sample could also have affected the result. The screen itself changed airflow and might have held warmth. No claim treats one season or one bed as a controlled laboratory experiment.

Talia kept the trial card with the wick readings and attached a note describing the watering delay. Anyone repeating the work should start both rows at the same time, use a marked measure for every watering, log temperature, and place the screen without changing drainage. If the counts converge under those conditions, that result must be kept too. If they diverge again, it would still be necessary to test the seed batch and water separately.

The badge Rowan received was cut from the brass tie used to keep both cards together. It has two parallel marks, one for each bed. It represents the obligation to carry both sides of a comparison forward, not a conclusion in favour of either one. Oren filed the method as a field trial with an explicit note that the missed hour remains a confounding variable. The data can guide a second attempt. It cannot justify reducing a ration, dismissing a grower's account or assigning blame to a water crew.

entries.title: Cinderwell: The Sheltered Trays
entries.body:
The sheltered repeat kept two nursery trays beneath one roof and divided a marked Salt Saffron lot between them. The trays were rotated between two shelves at night so that one position would not always receive the warmer air. Their planting times were recorded together. The aim was to repeat a small observation while using less of the exposed field, not to answer what the salt edge did to plants in a full bed.

A temperature strip showed that the tray nearest the vent warmed several marks at midday. The team began switching the trays after each evening count, but one swap was missed when the roof leaked. That interval stayed on the record. Germination counts were closer than those of the earlier mixed-position trays. The difference might come from the roof, repeated seed batch, more even timing or simply a small number of seeds. The team did not have enough matched trays to separate all of those factors.

Sister June noted that the roofed space was also needed to dry seed for the next ration season. Running more experiments there would have displaced sacks promised to growers. The chosen repeat therefore stopped at two trays. A future cycle can add a third temperature point if the storehouse has room, or return to the field beds after emergency distribution. Neither possibility guarantees that the next crop will survive.

The shelter cabinet was repaired with a round brass latch salvaged from a cracked tray frame. The clasp Rowan wears was made from its spare pin. It is a reminder to keep each sample protected and labeled, not a token proving that sheltered growth is safer for every seed lot. The labels preserve the batch, shelf, temperature, watering times and one missed position change. They leave room for a no-change result.

Oren attached a copy of the experiment plan to the front of the cabinet. Anyone opening it can see both the count and the limits before using the result. The notes cannot establish why the older sack behaved differently, where the salt in the furrow came from, or what share of basin water reached a field. They document one protected repeat that reduced the amount of soil used and narrowed some differences between trays. The outside bed remains a separate question for a time when land and seed can be spared.

entries.title: Quy ước thử Hai Hồi Chuông
entries.category: Sổ tay an toàn cộng đồng
entries.writtenBy: Harper Wills, với ghi chú của Mira Cole
entries.body:
Khung tín hiệu ở Ashfall từng dùng hai chiếc chuông khác cao độ. Trên giấy, một tiếng gọi đến giếng và hai tiếng gọi rời khỏi giếng là hai mệnh lệnh rõ ràng. Trong đêm cháy, tiếng gọi, tiếng mái đổ và gió ngang trộn lại. Harper đánh cả hai tín hiệu dồn dập, còn dân làng không có bản đồ chung. Không có ghi chép nào chứng minh một âm thanh duy nhất đã khiến gia đình ở ngõ đông quay lại; ký ức của Harper chỉ xác nhận bà đã đánh nhịp quá nhanh và tự trách mình sau đó.

Phấn Dấu Mưa được pha bằng một lá Moonwort nghiền cùng tro đồng đã sàng. Mẻ này để lại vệt nhìn thấy trên đá ướt và một gờ nhỏ có thể lần theo bằng ngón tay. Thử vệt ở giếng và gò đông sau khi gió đổi hướng. Ghi thời tiết, vị trí người quan sát, khoảng cách và thời điểm phấn nhòe. Tro chỉ là nguyên liệu màu; nó không thể xác định ai đã tháo chiếc chuông cũ.

Mỗi lần diễn tập phải có người tự nguyện ở ít nhất hai điểm, một bản đồ đặt cạnh khung và một đường đi thứ hai nếu dấu hiệu không đến được. Không kéo chuông khi có cháy thật để kiểm tra xem ai phản ứng; đêm đó không phải phòng thí nghiệm. Người dân có thể từ chối tham gia, yêu cầu xem bản ghi hoặc đề nghị sửa quy ước. Ghi nhận một lần thử thành công chỉ chứng minh tín hiệu hoạt động ở những vị trí đã thử, trong điều kiện được ghi lại.

entries.title: Nhịp Trầm, Khoảng Nghỉ
entries.body:
Quy ước ưu tiên của làng dùng một tiếng chuông trầm, một khoảng nghỉ dài, rồi hai tiếng trầm. Nhịp đầu yêu cầu người nghe dừng lại và nhìn bản đồ ở khung. Cặp nhịp sau chỉ hướng trở lại nơi trú; nó không có nghĩa mọi người phải chạy hoặc bỏ lại người bên cạnh. Không đánh liên tiếp để lấp đầy khoảng nghỉ. Nếu chuông bị gió che, có thể người ở mép giếng chỉ cảm thấy rung qua lan can hoặc không nhận được gì cả.

Bản hình của nhịp được ghim ở độ cao người ngồi cũng có thể đọc. Mỗi người tự chọn có muốn luyện tập hay không; sơ đồ vẫn ở nơi công cộng để ai cũng xem được mà không cần hỏi Harper. Người đưa tin tự nguyện có thể mang bản sao tới lối bắc vốn khuất tiếng. Không ghi tên người tham gia lên danh sách báo động, và không suy ra một hộ đã nhận tín hiệu chỉ vì nhà họ nằm trong vùng nghe được.

Harper thử nhịp từ lối nam và mép giếng trong một buổi mưa nhẹ. Gideon cảm thấy nhịp cuối ở lan can nhưng không nghe rõ các tiếng cao. Kết quả đó yêu cầu giữ một bảng hình dự phòng và ghi lại độ rung, chứ không chứng minh cả làng nghe thấy chuông. Kiểm tra trục, dây và dấu rỉ sau mưa lớn; nếu âm sắc đổi, tạm ngừng dùng nhịp cho tới khi mọi người được báo về thay đổi.

entries.title: Cờ Tam Giác Có Gân Nổi
entries.body:
Quy ước ưu tiên dùng một lá cờ tam giác có mép khuyết và hai gân nổi. Phần khuyết hướng về lối trở lại nơi trú; hai gân giúp phân biệt nó bằng đầu ngón tay khi ánh sáng yếu. Màu sáng và vệt tối chỉ tăng tương phản. Không ai cần phân biệt đỏ với xanh để hiểu hướng, và cũng không có tín hiệu nào yêu cầu người ta chạy. Cờ không phải lời xác nhận rằng nguy hiểm đã qua.

Ở lối nam, lá thử mở ra khi gió đổi chiều và một người quan sát nhận được cả hình tam giác lẫn mép khuyết. Từ sau vách giếng, không thể nhìn thấy cột. Mưa có thể dán vải vào thân cột; gió ngược có thể khiến mũi cờ chỉ sai hướng. Bản quy ước vì vậy phải đặt ngay cạnh cột, kèm sơ đồ đường về và tên người cần báo tin bằng lời nếu họ đứng ngoài tầm nhìn.

Gân nổi sẽ được may lại nếu bị rách, còn dây treo phải tháo xuống khi bão làm nó va vào cột. Người dân có thể tự cầm cờ, đề nghị một hình khác hoặc từ chối tham gia thử. Bản ghi đầu tiên chỉ mô tả hai điểm thử và thời tiết lúc đó; nó không khẳng định mọi góc trong làng đều nhìn thấy. Sau mỗi cơn mưa, một người tình nguyện kiểm tra độ bám, hình dạng và các góc khuất trước khi treo lại.

entries.title: Bảng Phấn Sau Cơn Mưa
entries.body:
Mira dùng ba cột vì ba câu hỏi cần ba câu trả lời. Ai đã được nhìn thấy sau khi mái kho sập? Ai xin chỗ ngủ trong hầm? Ai muốn ở lại tới sáng? Câu hỏi cuối không suy ra từ câu đầu. Một người có thể được nhìn thấy rồi tự rời đi, hoặc ở nhờ mà chưa biết mình sẽ lên đường.

Bên cạnh mỗi dấu, bảng ghi giờ và người xác nhận. Hai hàng để trống được giữ nguyên; Gideon không xóa chúng sau khi kể lại danh sách bằng trí nhớ. Mira treo bản chép cũ phía sau bảng mới thay vì giả làm như không có sai số.

Ghi chú này không phải sổ cư trú và cũng không đếm người đã chết. Người kiểm tra đã thấy một hành động ở một thời điểm; họ không nhìn theo mọi con đường. Nếu ai trở về với một sửa đổi, bản trước vẫn giúp xác định điều gì đổi và ai đã thay đổi nó. Một dòng trống có thể là dữ liệu chưa thu thập, quyền từ chối trả lời hoặc một câu hỏi chưa tới được đúng người. Không được chọn một nghĩa thay cho người chưa nói.

entries.title: Những Mảnh Bạt Không Mang Họ
entries.body:
Bốn miếng vải che cửa hầm được vá lại vào buổi sáng sau trận mưa. Gideon nhớ đường kim phải chạy xuôi theo độ dốc, nếu không nước sẽ tụ ở mép cửa. Mira nhớ hai đứa trẻ chọn các miếng theo màu để có thể phân biệt phía trong với phía ngoài khi trời tối. Cả hai ký ức giúp sửa mái. Không ký ức nào chỉ ra chính xác gia đình nào đã mang từng miếng đến.

Một người trong sân nói màu vàng đến từ nhà phía đông. Người khác đoán nó là vải bọc xe hàng. Tấm vải đã bị cắt nhỏ; đường viền cũ bị tháo; mưa đã cuốn trôi bụi ở mặt ngoài. Không còn phép đối chiếu đủ mạnh để chọn một lời kể.

Tôi ghi lại vật liệu đã dùng vì lần sửa tiếp theo sẽ cần biết số mảnh và chiều nước chảy. Tôi không viết tên hộ cạnh màu vải. Nếu chủ cũ muốn nhận ra phần của họ, họ có thể tự nói; một miếng vá không thể thay họ làm việc đó. Trên trang sau, tôi ghi thêm hai lỗ kim mới để người giữ hầm kiểm tra mái sau cơn bão.

Bạt giữ người khỏi mưa trong đêm ấy. Nó không chứng minh ai đã ở trong hầm, ai còn ở ngoài làng hay ai đã chọn ra đi. Vật hữu ích có thể được giữ lại mà không biến thành nhân chứng giả.

entries.title: Quy Tắc Cho Bản Đường Rời Làng
entries.body:
Một bản đường sơ tán có thể giúp người mới tới tìm thấy giếng, cửa hầm và lối xe kéo. Nếu bản được treo ở sân, nhiều người có thể chỉ ra đoạn đường đã sạt hoặc dòng chỉ dẫn không còn đúng. Khả năng sửa công khai cũng có cái giá: người đọc có thể đoán hộ nào đang ở phía sau mỗi ngõ cụt, nhất là khi trên bản đồ còn sót tên người ghi. Vì vậy Rowan chừa phần nhận diện hộ khỏi bản treo và ghi ngày cho từng lần sửa.

Phiếu riêng giữ quyền quyết định trong tay mỗi nhà. Một người có thể cất tờ giấy, đưa cho người thân hoặc yêu cầu một đường đi khác mà không để lại bản sao đầy đủ ở quảng trường. Nhưng nếu hai phiếu mô tả cùng một ngã rẽ khác nhau, người kiểm tra không có bản chung để nhìn thấy sai lệch. Khi đó người mang phiếu phải tự chọn có muốn đem chúng tới đối chiếu hay không.

Không cách nào hứa rằng bản đồ sẽ đúng mãi. Bản chung cần một quy trình sửa và dấu ngày rõ ràng; phiếu riêng cần nơi hỏi lại khi người giữ muốn trao đổi. Cả hai cách đều bỏ qua một giả định: rằng người nhận có thể đọc, giữ và sử dụng tờ giấy mà không gặp nguy hiểm. Gideon vì thế ghi số phiếu đã phát nhưng không ghi tên hộ trong tổng số ấy.

Sự lựa chọn ở Ashfall không quyết định ai đáng tin hơn. Nó lưu lại điều cộng đồng chấp nhận chia sẻ lúc họ đang cần rời chỗ trú. Bản cũ vẫn được giữ sau bản mới. Nếu người về sau muốn thay đổi quy tắc, họ cần ngày sửa, lý do, người đã đồng thuận và cách nhận khiếu nại; một con số tăng lên không thể tự kể câu chuyện của mọi nhà.

entries.title: Seal Log for the Return Case
entries.body:
I carried the field case back through the aperture with its brass latch wrapped in sailcloth. The cloth was not evidence of damage. It was a promise to the people who had packed the instruments that I would not open the container until another observer could watch.

The outer seal is mine. The inner wax is not. A narrow crescent has been pressed into it, then covered by a second layer. I cannot tell whether the first mark was made before or after the case was moved. I have written both possibilities in the margin and left the date blank until Evelyn checks the resin.

There are four shallow hollows in the felt insert. They show where tools rested; they do not tell us who carried each tool. The inventory page has four lines, but only my handwriting appears on the last. A missing name is not proof that a person left, died, or refused to sign. It is proof that the page does not contain that name.

For years I kept the box closed because I thought opening it would make me choose one explanation for the expedition. It does not. The latch can open while the conclusion stays unresolved. Anyone who handles the case after me should record the state of each seal before touching the contents.

entries.title: Four Hollows, No Names
entries.body:
The felt insert has four depressions around a central ring. One is deeper along its western edge, as if a narrow tool was lifted out while the case tilted. The cut could come from a wrench, a sample tube, or a buckle on the carrying strap. No measurement distinguishes those objects.

A pencil line connects the four hollows to a route scratched into the case lid. The route bends toward the sealed aperture, then stops at the hinge. It may mark the direction in which the case was carried. It may also be a repair guide left by someone who did not go on the expedition.

Jace recognizes the cut in the felt as his own work. He says he shaped the insert to stop the wind needles knocking together. That account explains the central ring; it does not identify the objects at the four edges. Evelyn has asked him to keep the distinction visible.

The archive will not assign a hollow to a person. The crew roster remains incomplete, and the felt cannot repair it. What it can do is show that several instruments traveled together and that somebody took care to keep them from breaking.

entries.title: Clock Drift by Temperature
entries.body:
The old wind mast uses a steel spring exposed to the room air. In the coldest recorded interval, the spring shortened enough to delay the pointer by approximately one beat on the water clock. The field note gives a range, not a single correction, because the mast temperature was not measured at the same moment as the signal.

Jace's earlier report records a seventeen-beat delay between the first sound and the vane turning. The clock used for that count is unknown. The new trial with a separate sand timer produced a delay between sixteen and eighteen beats. Those intervals overlap. This supports the possibility that the old vane moved after the sound, but it cannot establish what moved the air.

We have preserved the old spring in its original position and placed a second indicator beside it. A future observer can compare them without overwriting the first trace. The instrument is less tidy than the diagram in the archive. That is acceptable: a clean diagram must not hide the condition of the equipment that produced the result.

entries.title: Farwake Carp: A Humidity Witness
entries.body:
The silver scales of a Farwake Carp hold a fine moisture film after the fish leaves Celestial Pool. Evelyn uses that film to test how quickly the replacement membrane responds when a damp current passes over it. The fish is a calibration sample for the instrument, not a message from the water.

The first reading varies with the time the sample spends in open air. We have therefore recorded the catch time, the distance from the pool, and the temperature beside each trial. When the scales dry, the response becomes weaker. That change tells us about moisture on the membrane; it does not explain the old wind direction.

Jace wanted to write that the fish reacted to the incoming signal. We repeated the trial with the receiver switched off. The scales still changed as they dried. He crossed out the causal sentence himself and kept the observation.

A good sample is allowed to disappoint the person who brought it in. It is more useful to know what it can measure than to give it a story it cannot support.

entries.title: Jace Morrow: First Account
entries.body:
The sound came through the arch during a period when the outer shutters were vibrating. One member of the party recognized a familiar name. Another heard a metal edge scraping. A third asked us to stop the recording because the noise was making it hard to breathe. The original log records those reactions in the order they were spoken, but the later summary replaced them with one phrase: “voices of the dead.”

Jace says he used that phrase because the group needed to leave the chamber at once. The western floor had cracked, and a wounded surveyor could not walk without help. He believed that the evacuation order would be acted on faster if the sound were treated as a danger. He also knew that the vane had moved after the first noise.

Both statements can be true. A quick evacuation may have been necessary; the summary may still have erased meaningful differences between what people heard. This record does not decide whether Jace's choice was justified. It preserves the choice, its stated reason, and the measurements that existed at the time.

entries.title: Independent Trial Sheet
entries.body:
The replacement wind membrane is to be tested alongside the old vane. Neither instrument may be removed before the other has recorded one full interval. A third observer will mark the temperature and a separate water clock will count beats.

The trial is invalid if the aperture changes position during the reading, if the receiver transmits, or if the pool surface is disturbed by a nearby actor. A failed trial should remain in the notebook with the reason for failure. We will not discard it simply because the needle did not behave as expected.

Jace asked whether the experiment could prove the source of the sound. It cannot. At best it can establish whether air moved toward the inner chamber and whether the instruments agree about the direction. Identifying a source would require a new measurement from beyond the aperture, and nobody has permission to risk another expedition on a conclusion this narrow.

The purpose of repeating the observation is not to make the old crew agree with us. It is to give future observers a way to challenge our reading.

entries.title: North Window Weather Record
entries.body:
The north record names the hour and cloud cover, then omits the direction of the glass. On the reverse, an arrow points toward the sealed aperture. A line below it reads “no eastern door,” which may describe the room rather than the weather.

During the original survey, the shutters were closed on the eastern wall. The only movable panel faced the aperture. If a current entered through a seam, the room could have turned it before it reached the vane. The report contains no pressure reading near the floor and none above the arch.

We have added two blank columns: “observer position” and “open surfaces.” They are not corrections to the old page. They mark information that was not collected. A blank column is more honest than reconstructing a room from an arrow.

Jace has asked that the arrow remain visible in public copies. He once wanted it removed because it seemed to promise a direction. Now he says a reader should be allowed to see the mark and its limits together.

entries.title: Second Wind Membrane: Assembly Note
entries.body:
The membrane uses a thin sheet of cured Skyroot sap stretched over a fish-scale frame. The Skyroot takes small changes in pressure without tearing. The curved scales spread the movement across the frame. This design is not a transmitter; the membrane is attached to a passive register and has no power coil.

The recipe calls for one portion of sap and one Farwake Carp. The sap should be warmed until it bends without clouding. The fish is cleaned after the calibration sample has been taken. No part of the animal is preserved as a symbol; its contribution is a measurable surface tension.

Jace suggested setting the new membrane to match the old vane. Evelyn refused. The two instruments should retain independent calibrations so that agreement means something. If their readings diverge, we will inspect the mounts before adjusting either one.

This device cannot determine whether a sound is speech. It can record pressure changes and the time at which the vane turns. That narrow purpose is a safeguard, not a flaw.

entries.title: Passive Receiver Interval
entries.body:
The receiver remained in listening mode throughout the trial. Its power indicator stayed dark, and the antenna was disconnected from the outbound coil. The membrane registered one movement after the sound, but the time of the movement fell within the cold-clock range recorded on the previous sheet.

No distinct return signal appeared during the next ten minutes. We have not labeled the silence as refusal or absence. The equipment may not have been sensitive enough; a distant device may have been inactive; there may have been no device at all.

The first report treated silence as an answer because the crew had to leave the aperture. This report records silence as a condition of the trial. The distinction gives later observers room to test another interval without inheriting our expectation.

The receiver's passive state is written in three places: the panel mark, Jace's clock, and Rowan's copy. A future reader should be able to notice if those records fail to match.

entries.title: The Two Layers of the Report
entries.body:
Under the final sentence, the draft reads “wind from outside.” The darker ink above it reads “voices of the dead.” Both phrases are in Jace's hand. The paper fibers show that the first sentence was not erased; it was covered.

Jace cannot remember whether he changed the words before or after the evacuation order. He remembers the pressure of the pen and the sound of the western floor splitting. He does not remember who first said the name they thought they heard. Those gaps should remain gaps.

The signature at the bottom verifies that Jace approved the final page. It does not verify that every crew member agreed with its description. The absence of other signatures is not evidence of protest, consent, or death. It is a limit of the document.

A copy has been made with both ink layers traced separately. The archive keeps the original flat and untouched. Readers may compare the sentences without treating either as a complete record of the expedition.

entries.title: Statement Options and Limits
entries.body:
Jace has chosen between two ways to amend the public record. The first is a signed first-person account. It places responsibility for the final wording beside the person who wrote and approved it, while preserving the possibility that the account may later be challenged.

The second is a methods record containing instrument settings, temperatures, clock tolerances, and the observer positions. Jace's identity remains on the sealed original but is not used as a substitute for testimony from the rest of the party.

Neither option restores the words that were omitted. Neither identifies the source of the sound. The signed account may help readers understand an emergency decision; the methods record may help them repeat a measurement. Their different purposes should not be collapsed into one document.

Any member of the old crew who returns may request a correction to their own statement. No one else is authorized to invent that correction for them.

entries.title: Signed Account: Jace Morrow
entries.body:
I opened the aperture while the wind was still moving. I left the observation room to help one injured person reach the lower passage. When I returned, the needle had shifted and the recorder had stopped.

I believed a frightening sentence would make the others evacuate more quickly. I chose the phrase “voices of the dead” because it was stronger than “sound of unknown origin.” The report needed a clear hazard. The sentence also made people believe we had heard the same thing, which we had not.

I cannot say what the other surveyors heard. I cannot say whether they agreed with my warning. I cannot write what they would forgive. I can name the choice I made and let them add their own accounts if they ever wish to.

This statement is mine. It is not a group confession, a witness list, or an answer about what lies beyond the Veil.

entries.title: Open Method Card: Wind Membrane Trial
entries.body:
Observers: Rowan Hale and Dr. Evelyn Hart. Instrument custodian: Jace Morrow. The original wind vane remained mounted. A second passive membrane was tested beside it after the room temperature fell below the previous day's reading.

The membrane shifted between sixteen and eighteen beats after the first recorded sound. The vane shifted within the same interval. The old report gives seventeen beats but does not name its clock. The results overlap once the stated clock tolerance is included.

The receiver did not transmit during the trial. No distinct return signal was detected in the following ten minutes. The test cannot identify a speaker or prove that anyone heard the signal. It can be repeated with a warmer spring, a second water clock, and observers standing at opposite ends of the chamber.

Jace's signed account is stored separately. This card gives a reader the method without asking that reader to accept his interpretation.

entries.title: A Place at the Table Without Minutes
entries.body:
Jace set four cups around the stove and left one empty. He did not say the cup belonged to a missing crew member. He said the cup was there in case somebody wanted tea after coming in from the cold.

The group ate without writing down who took the last piece of bread. Evelyn told a story about a measurement she had ruined by leaning on a tripod. Jace laughed, then corrected the temperature she remembered. Neither correction entered the official archive.

Before leaving, Jace placed a blank page in the return case. Its heading says “If someone comes back.” Below it are three empty fields: words they want preserved, words they want removed, and whether they want their name attached.

The page has no deadline. The archive is not entitled to fill it in while it remains blank.

entries.title: The Margin Melody
entries.body:
The melody on the chime rubbing is written in wax, not cut into the stone. The strokes have the uneven spacing of a person learning a tune by listening rather than reading notes. The melody begins with two descending tones, leaves a long rest, and rises by a half-step.

No name accompanies it. The wax was added after the surrounding stone had been catalogued, but before the edge was polished. We cannot tell whether the writer meant the tune for a ceremony or for private practice.

Lyra recognizes the sequence as a song she began years ago while swimming between the lower archive and the surface. She stopped writing it when she became responsible for preserving the older tablets. The mark survived because nobody had entered it into the official register.

The archive records this as Lyra's work after she confirmed authorship. It does not attach the tune to any of the dead voices stored nearby.

entries.title: Lyra Moss: A Voice Kept Outside the Ledger
entries.body:
When I was young, the elders taught me to listen before I spoke. That was good advice. In the archive, it became a rule that I should listen forever and leave my own voice out of the record.

I followed the rule because I was afraid of changing the tablets. The stones had survived fire, water, and people who wanted their version of history to be the only one. I thought adding myself would be another kind of damage.

But the tune in the margin is not a correction to an old account. It is a new song. I wrote it about the path to the surface and the moment the water turns silver. I do not want it mistaken for testimony, and I do not want it to disappear because I work here.

A keeper can protect a shelf and still belong to the room. I am trying to learn that without making the room answer for me.

entries.title: Whisper Koi Sound Sample
entries.body:
Lyra uses the reflective scales of a Whisper Koi to compare how a note changes after passing through water. The sample captures a range of pitches; it does not translate them into words.

The scale is placed beside the same tuning fork twice, once before the pool settles and once after. The second reading is quieter. A small movement in the water changes the reflection enough to alter the measurement. The notebook marks this as a property of the room, not the intention of the fish.

Several archive entries describe the Whisper Koi as carrying lost voices. Those phrases belong to older folklore and remain part of the collection, but they are not used as labels for this sample. The present record concerns resonance, water depth, and the angle of the lamp.

A listener may find the tone beautiful or unsettling. Neither reaction changes the data.

entries.title: Two Listeners, One Recording
entries.body:
The playback log contains two descriptions of the same ten-second recording. One listener wrote “oar against stone.” The other wrote “a low tide turning under the arch.” Both were standing in the choir room, and neither could see the device during playback.

The difference does not make one person careless. The first listener had worked on the lake; the second had spent years in the lower archive. Their memories shaped the words they chose. The recording itself contains a low vibration and three short peaks. It does not contain enough information to establish the cause.

Lyra's older procedure asked the keeper to select one description for the catalogue. Her new procedure preserves both, adds the measured waveform, and invites a third listener who has not read either note. The keeper is no longer required to decide which memory sounds more authoritative.

The record is useful because it shows the boundaries between sound, description, and interpretation.

entries.title: The First Warden on the Listening Oath
entries.body:
The first listening oath was written after the archive lost an entire night of testimony. I remember the arguments but not the names of everyone who spoke. The surviving stone says only that silence must not be taken for consent.

It does not say every voice must be stored. It does not say a keeper should be absent from the record. We wrote the oath to keep the powerful from calling a frightened silence agreement. We did not write it to forbid new songs.

I have repeated the words for so long that I can forget they were a beginning, not a complete law. Lyra may add a tune if she names it as her own. A listener may decline to hear it. The archive may hold a copy only under the permission its author gives.

I cannot grant that permission for her. I can tell her that the oath leaves the decision in her hands.

entries.title: Invitation for an Optional Listening
entries.body:
The invitation is addressed to no one by name. It says that Lyra Moss has written a short melody and would like to perform it for listeners who choose to attend. A visitor can leave at any point without explanation.

The sign-in sheet records only the names of people who ask to be named. The recording form is separate from the attendance form. Someone may hear the song without permitting a copy to be kept; someone else may allow a copy while asking that their reaction stay private.

Two visitors left before the final phrase. The playback copy includes the interval where they departed, but does not identify them. Their absence is not recorded as criticism or fear. It is simply the end of their participation.

Lyra has authorized one public performance and one recording of her own voice. She has not granted permission to use any other sound from the archive.

entries.title: Instrumental Copy with a Protected Verse
entries.body:
Lyra placed the page containing her melody in a small box with a date for review. The two keys are held separately. The box can be opened by Lyra, or by a future keeper after she has renewed the permission herself.

The public copy contains the rhythm and the instrumental notes but leaves the vocal line empty. The empty staff is not a transcription error. It is an intentional space that a later musician may fill with an original phrase of their own.

The score does not invite anyone to guess Lyra's hidden tune. The protected verse belongs to her whether or not the archive ever hears it. The Choir can preserve a work without claiming access to every part of its maker.

This arrangement is not permanent. Lyra may release the verse, revise the score, or ask for the public copy to be withdrawn. The date is a reminder to ask, not an automatic expiration.

entries.title: Lyra's Next Song Is Not an Archive Record
entries.body:
Lyra says the next melody may be about a kitchen lamp, a slippery stair, or the way Echo Kelp smells when it is ready to harvest. She does not know yet. She has given herself permission to write something that contains no witness and no conclusion.

The archive has filed the choice about her first song. It has not filed the conversation that followed, because Lyra asked us not to turn every moment into a record. Rowan keeps the small brass tuning fork she lent him and will return it when he comes back.

If Lyra performs the song for willing listeners, their permissions will be stored separately. If she keeps it private, nobody will treat the closed box as evidence that she regrets writing it.

The record ends here. The tune does not have to.

entries.title: Glassplum Graft: First Cut
entries.body:
The cành ghép was wrapped in linen when I found it beneath the old north trellis. It had no label, so I placed a temporary tag on the stake instead of naming the plant. The cut at the join is clean on one side and rough on the other. Whoever made it knew how to graft, but the blade slipped near the lower root.

I chose the name Glassplum because the first surviving fruit had a clear rind and a small stone. It is a working name. A person who helped tend the old garden may remember another one, and they are welcome to tell us. The label can change without erasing this entry.

Two seeds are set aside for the first trial. One will be planted in the mixed soil bed; the second remains dry as a reserve. If only one germinates, the ledger will say so. I will not call the second seed “lost” until we know it was used.

Rowan brought the seed packet back with its corners folded flat. I have noted the date, the bed, and the fact that the packet was opened by two people.

entries.title: Names Before Yield Totals
entries.body:
My aunt kept the old root garden through the winter when the outer beds failed. She taught me that a crop ledger is not just a count of baskets. It is a way to remember who carried water while another person was ill, who saved seed when a harvest looked too small, and who asked to stop tending a plot.

I write a name only when the person wants it there. Some people prefer a household mark; some want no name attached. The ledger has a blank column for that choice, and the blank stays blank unless the gardener asks me to fill it.

The Glassplum branch came from that garden. I do not know whether my aunt grafted it or whether another keeper did. The first record has a fruit drawing but no date. I have copied the drawing into the new page and written “origin unknown” beneath it.

A missing name cannot be recovered by a guess, even a kind guess. If somebody returns with the old name, I will place it beside the working one and record who supplied it.

entries.title: First Glassplum Harvest
entries.body:
The first Glassplum harvest contains two intact fruits and one with a split rind. The split appeared after a cold night. All three grew on the same branch, but the soil at the western edge held more water than the center of the bed.

Mara has asked that the damaged fruit stay in the record. Removing it would make the crop look more reliable than it was. She measures the weight of each fruit, records the position on the branch, and notes the temperature before sunrise.

The two intact fruits have a thin glassy skin and pale flesh. The split fruit has no sign of rot. It may still be useful in a cooked recipe, but that has not been tested yet. The harvest is small; it does not tell us whether the plant can feed a household or survive a dry season.

One successful plant is a reason to repeat the trial, not a reason to distribute every seed in storage.

entries.title: Season Card with Failed Buds
entries.body:
The old card marks three early blossoms with a blue stroke and then crosses out the expected harvest date. A note says the night air turned cold before dawn. There is no count of fruit because none remained on the branch.

The same card records that water was redirected toward the Moonwort bed. The choice was made by two caretakers who signed their names. It was not an accident and not a hidden order. They needed medicine leaves for the sickroom and believed the Glassplum could wait.

I have copied the crossing-out exactly. If I rewrite the card as “failed crop,” a reader might think the plant itself was at fault. If I write only “water redirected,” the reader may miss what the caretakers gave up. Both details belong together.

The next trial will keep a small reserve of water for the graft. It will not take water away from the herb bed without an agreed review.

entries.title: Soil Tray Comparison
entries.body:
Two trays were filled from opposite sides of the well. The western tray holds moisture longer but develops a hard skin when it dries. The central tray loses water sooner and keeps a loose surface. Mara says the difference follows the old root channel, not the crop line.

We did not add dye to the water because nobody had tested whether the dye would harm the trial fruit. Instead, Rowan measured the time before the top layer stopped shining. The measurement is rough; it depends on how close the lamp is and on who decides that the shine has ended.

The new page records the lamp position and the observer. A later gardener can repeat the observation under the same conditions or disagree with our threshold. The result does not prove that one soil is better. It only shows that the two parts of the bed dry at different rates.

Mara has left the water channel unchanged until the second harvest is compared.

entries.title: Rootglass Syrup: Small Batch Note
entries.body:
Two Glassplum fruits and one measure of Skyroot sap make a small batch of Rootglass Syrup. The fruits are simmered until the skins soften; the sap is added after the pot leaves the flame so the mixture does not cloud.

The recipe began as a drink for gardeners who had worked through the warmest part of the day. It may restore some strength when a traveler is tired. It is not a remedy for fever, infection, or injuries. The label on the jar includes that limit so nobody carries the syrup to a sickroom as a promise.

The first batch smells of green wood and sour fruit. Mara tasted one spoon and wrote down the hour, the ingredients, and her own name. Rowan described it as “bright,” which is a personal impression rather than a measure. Both notes can remain beside the recipe.

If the next batch tastes different, the page will record the difference instead of correcting it.

entries.title: Two Harvests on One Root
entries.body:
The second harvest came from the same plant after the first branch was pruned. Two fruits remained whole; one split along the seam where the skin met the stem. The western soil stayed wet longer after a brief rain, and the central soil dried before evening.

The first and second batches were not grown under identical conditions. Rowan removed a damaged support stake between them, and the sky was cloudier during the second growth. This means the comparison can help plan another trial but cannot establish a single cause for the cracked fruit.

Mara has kept all of the weights, including the small fruit that would not fit the usual basket. She says a small yield is still part of a crop's life. The ledger now has a column for branches that were pruned and another for plants that were left untouched.

The third season should be decided with the neighboring gardeners, because their beds share the same root channel.

entries.title: Late Bloom at the Graft
entries.body:
A pale root has grown beyond the original graft and entered the lower soil on its own. It is thinner than the old rootstock but no longer depends entirely on the upper branch for water. The join has not separated.

Mara marks this as a new observation rather than “proof of independence.” One root was visible today; the rest remain under the soil. Digging them out would disturb the plant, so the next check will wait until after the cold season.

A leaf held frost along its edge for several minutes after sunrise. The rest of the plant remained upright. We have recorded the time and air temperature, but the frost could have formed on the leaf because it was sheltered from the wind. We do not know whether the cultivar has unusual resistance.

The plant has survived two harvests. That is enough to continue the trial and not enough to promise anyone a reliable crop.

entries.title: Glassplum Seed Sharing Charter
entries.body:
Three households have asked to test Glassplum on their own plots. Each will receive one seed and a card with the water limit, the time of planting, and the two earlier harvest records. They can refuse the seed or return it unused.

The trial asks for a note on whether the seed germinates and whether the plant affects nearby roots. It does not require a name, a photograph, or a public account of who planted it. The community summary may include totals if enough participants agree, but an individual household can request that its measurements remain private.

A gardener may stop the trial if the plant competes with food crops or needs more water than expected. Stopping is not recorded as failure. It is recorded as a safety decision and may prevent the same problem from reaching another bed.

Mara will review the charter after the cold season with the people who accepted seeds. The review date is part of the permission.

entries.title: Rootstock Held for One More Season
entries.body:
The original rootstock remains in the Greenwake trial bed. The reserve seeds are dry in a jar with two separate keys. The jar label gives a review date after the next cold season and lists the neighbors invited to attend.

Keeping the rootstock does not guarantee that the plant will thrive. It delays distribution while Mara watches whether the late frost changes the next harvest and whether nearby roots remain unaffected. Households who asked for seed have received the present measurements and can choose another crop while they wait.

The jar can be opened early if the bed becomes unsafe or if the caretakers agree that waiting causes more harm than the uncertain trial. The rule is written on the outside so no one must break the seal to learn what it permits.

A delay can become a quiet refusal if nobody reviews it. The date prevents that from happening invisibly. It does not force Mara to share the seeds; it requires her to answer the people who asked.

entries.title: A Garden Need Not Prove Its Worth
entries.body:
Mara plans to plant a row of trees for shade beside the west path. The fruit may be small, late, or absent. She does not intend to remove the row if it fails to improve a harvest.

Her aunt used to say a garden needs both food and places to sit. In the old ledger, those two purposes were separated into different books, as if shade were not part of keeping people alive through a hot afternoon. Mara has begun a new page with both columns visible.

The Glassplum trial remains active whether the seeds were shared or held back. One route gives more gardeners a chance to learn; the other protects the original plant while another season is observed. The page records which choice was made and when it can be reviewed.

A future reader may decide the choice was wrong. The record leaves room for that reader to say so.

entries.title: The Shift Book with a Blank Hour
entries.body:
The first page records where each watch stood and which key they carried. The column marked rest is empty. A later hand has written a small dash beside two names, then scratched both marks until only the paper is rough.

Alden says the book belonged to a rotation after the old floodgate was repaired. He remembers using the empty hours to work on his sword, but does not remember who took his place. His memory is not a second copy of the ledger.

The cover does not explain whether the blank column means nobody rested or nobody thought rest belonged in the record. We have left the heading as it is and added a question in the margin. No answer has been entered on behalf of the people whose names remain inside.

Supplemental Last Oath archive note —Supplemental Last Oath archive note — leave the blank hour unresolved

Mara compares the shift book with the small fuel tally kept beside the floodgate. The tally shows that someone added kindling during the missing hour, but it does not identify who rested or whether the watch changed hands. Alden first wants to copy the mark into the rest column. Nia asks him to preserve it as a separate observation with its own source. The blank remains on the original page, while the fuel note is indexed next to it. A person may have tended the gate without signing the roster; the book does not settle that question. The new copy makes the gap easier to see, not easier to fill.

entries.title: A Commander Is Not a Reserve Roster
entries.body:
For years I believed that if a gate remained guarded, the order had succeeded. I counted open hours and measured the width of the patrol line. I did not count the time a guard had been awake before taking the post, or the walk home after leaving it.

A commander can arrange another person to stand at a gate. He cannot decide that the person is willing to do so. A roster that contains a replacement without a request is another order, not evidence of consent.

I have written three questions on the inside cover: who asked to trade, who approved the exchange, and how a person could leave without being called disloyal. I have no names for the old shifts. The questions must remain useful even when the answers cannot be recovered.

Supplemental Last Oath archive note —Supplemental Last Oath archive note — commander, take the first unassigned shift

During the test rotation, the hour before dawn has no volunteer. Alden offers to take it himself, then asks the people already present whether his doing so would prevent anyone from requesting a later change. They agree to try the shift once, with a rest period afterward and no penalty if the hour proves difficult. Alden records himself as the person on duty, not as the person who assigned it. The distinction matters to him because he has spent years using an order as a substitute for asking. One night of a different practice cannot rewrite the old ledger, but it gives the next keeper a procedure to review.

entries.title: A Root That Waited Through the Frost
entries.body:
One Emberroot seed was planted beside the north wall before dusk. The top soil was dry when it went in. A thin layer of frost appeared on the stone after midnight, while the bed remained sheltered beneath the roof edge.

The plant survived to harvest. This is one observation from one protected bed. It does not show how an exposed seed would behave, and it does not prove that Emberroot can replace a meal or keep someone warm during a watch.

The old schedule listed fuel, food and guard hours on separate pages. Mara has copied the planting date onto the reverse of the watch sheet so that a future reader can see which conditions were present. She has not combined the crop yield with the number of people on duty.

Supplemental Last Oath archive note —Supplemental Last Oath archive note — keep the frost line beside the watering time

The gardener returns to the bed before sunrise and finds a white line of frost on the outside stone, but none on the soil under the roof edge. Rowan compares the mark with the watering card and sees that the bed was watered earlier than the exposed plot. They record both facts without claiming that the shelter alone protected the plant. The gardener asks to keep one living root in the soil until the next shift can inspect it. Alden writes the request beside the harvest date and removes the root from his supply estimate. The crop trial can continue only if the person tending it chooses to continue.

entries.title: A Fish at the End of the Quiet Hour
entries.body:
The Starlit Minnow took the bait once the surface stopped trembling. I wrote down the time, the cloud cover and the number of ripples near the southern post. The fish did not appear on the next cast.

Alden had marked this hour as suitable for relief in the old book, but the minnow cannot verify his schedule. The catch tells us only that one fish was present under these conditions. We should not promise that the lake will provide food on a night when the watch is hungry.

The sample was used in a small metal-and-root spindle. Its value is as a dated observation and a test of the craft, not as a signal to begin a shift.

Supplemental Last Oath archive note —Supplemental Last Oath archive note — schedule the rest even when no fish is caught

On the next cast, Rowan waits through the same quiet interval and brings back no Minnow. Alden notices that the shift book has a field for catch and no field for the time spent beside the water. He adds a separate observation for an empty hook and a line for the fisher's rest period. No one has to cast again to earn a break. The lake may offer no food, and the quiet hour still belongs to the person who stood watch. Alden crosses out a note suggesting that the catch could supply a night meal. A single successful cast never made the schedule dependable.

entries.title: The Removable Spindle
entries.body:
The spindle holds a page at two corners without piercing the paper. A strip of treated Emberroot forms its center; a fish-scale washer keeps the wire from cutting through the grain. The parts can be taken apart with a fingernail.

The device can mark which revision is being read. It cannot mark who agreed to the schedule. Alden has been told to leave the signature field beside the person taking the shift, not beneath the commander’s seal.

If a family asks to remove its copy, the spindle releases the page without tearing it. This is a modest design feature, but the older binder made removal impossible. A record that cannot be withdrawn can outlive the permission that created it.

Supplemental Last Oath archive note —Supplemental Last Oath archive note — release the page before filing a correction

Nia demonstrates the spindle by turning its two grips until the watch sheet lifts free without tearing. She marks the original page number on its sleeve, then places a correction beside it rather than stitching the new page into the old one. Alden asks whether a loose page could be lost. Nia adds a return slot and a receipt so the person who takes it can bring it back or request a copy. The tool protects paper, not the truth of every line. Its value is that a reader can remove a record for review without destroying the revision trail or the original's custody history.

entries.title: One Sword Mark, One Person
entries.body:
I made the grooves on my sword while the watch was quiet. The cuts are uneven because I was tired. I used them to count the nights I personally stayed near the gate, and for a long time I treated that count as proof that the gate had always been covered.

It proves no such thing. The marks belong to me. I know why I made them because I remember the work. A similar cut on another weapon would not tell me who made it, whether they were awake, or whether they wanted the post.

I have placed a drawing of the grooves next to the schedule. The drawing is labeled “Alden’s sword,” not “the guard’s mark.” The distinction should survive copying.

Supplemental Last Oath archive note —Supplemental Last Oath archive note — stop counting nights with the blade

Alden puts the sword away after the tracing is made. He used to touch the grooves whenever he believed he had stayed longer than the other guards. The marks became a private way of proving that he had carried the duty alone. When Rowan shows him the missing hour in the ledger, he sees how the blade's count left no room for anyone else's unrecorded work. He does not cut new grooves to represent them; that would turn his guess into their evidence. The tracing remains labeled with Alden's name and explanation. The other workers may submit their own account or leave the page untouched.

entries.title: A Cycle Name Is Not a Shift Signature
entries.body:
The final roll was made to preserve the names called into the cycle. It was not designed as a record of consent to each task performed by those people. The watch book was written by another office and answers a different question: who stood at a gate during a given hour.

When later archivists stacked these documents together, the headings were treated as interchangeable. They are not. A person can be named in a cycle roll and still have refused a particular shift. A blank watch column does not remove a person from history, and a filled one does not reveal why they were present.
