The note will remind the next cook that heavy work can change what a person wants, without turning one worker into a spokesperson for the entire crew.

Someone else asks to keep the recipe as it is because they liked the first bowl. June leaves both comments where the cook can see them. Rowan suggests tallying each preference, but June points out that the people who had to leave before supper never had a chance to reply. The record describes who spoke, in broad terms, and when the meal was served. It remains a small sample. June will offer the recipe again and accept new notes without requiring anyone to defend an earlier choice. Feedback can alter the next pot; it cannot close the conversation.

entries.title: Road Meal Handoff
entries.body:
The crew secured one serving for travel and chose its carrier among themselves. June did not assign the bowl to a particular person or add it to the cargo count as a person marker. The handoff is complete when the food leaves the kitchen under the crew's care. Its eventual use remains with the travelers, who may eat, share or pass it on.

Supplemental Cinderwell kitchen note — the crew owns the handoff after departure

The crew chooses a carrier and checks that the crate latch opens from both sides. June records the serving's departure time because a warm bowl should not sit sealed for hours. She does not ask the carrier to report who eventually ate it. The handoff ends at the gate; after that, the travelers decide how to share the food.

Rowan's page describes the container and the portion, not a person. A future count of meals can compare what left the kitchen with what remained in the pot, but it cannot infer the crew's route or destination. The road stays open beyond this little supply record.

Second hearing — a handoff ends where the road begins

The crew returns with the basket after two days, scraped along one side and still usable. They say the bowl reached the first camp, but they do not know who ate from it after their own watch changed. June asks whether the latch worked and whether the wrapping kept the container steady. They answer those questions and leave the rest untold. She thanks them without asking for a route map or a list of names.

Rowan adds that the handoff is confirmed to the gate and that a later camp was reported by the carrier. He does not write that the meal reached every traveler. June approves the narrower note. In the kitchen, a report can end at the limit of what the reporter saw without being called incomplete or unhelpful. The returned basket lets them plan another serving; the uncertain journey remains with the people who made it. June hangs the receipt beside the packing card so the next crew can choose a lighter wrap, not so the kitchen can follow them farther than they agreed.

entries.title: Afterword: A Kitchen Without a Roll Call
entries.body:
June keeps the portable brazier available for another meal service. The first pot connected a local crop, a caught fish and a cooking station, while the branch decision determined whether its first bowl stayed with the kitchen shift or traveled with the road crew. Rowan retains a second bowl as a usable healing item. The kitchen's continued use depends on the people who choose to come back; this entry does not promise steady food supply or repair the cracked permanent hearth.

Supplemental Cinderwell kitchen note — the kitchen waits for its next cook

June stores the brazier where the next shift can inspect its legs before lighting it. The recipe hangs inside a clean sleeve, with the hearth crack and current draft card beside it. She asks Oren to tell her when another kitchen packet is ready, but does not reserve grain without his agreement.

The first service made two bowls and gave Rowan one usable item. It did not rebuild the permanent hearth, produce a stable yield or answer how many people need food each day. June will reopen the table when someone chooses to cook and the pantry can spare ingredients.

Second hearing — a place for the person who opens tomorrow

At the end of the week, June leaves the kitchen key on its peg and writes the name of the next cook only after that person agrees to take it. The recipe sleeve is clean. The hearth still needs its full inspection, and the pantry card still calls for another check. Nothing on the board declares the room finished. June finds this comforting: a completed quest can mark one good handoff without pretending the community has stopped changing.

Rowan asks whether she is disappointed that the kitchen is smaller than the old public hall. June looks at the benches and says size is not the same as welcome. A room can feed people well and still need more hands; the next shift may decide to expand, pause or cook something else. She wants the archive to leave that decision open. The current pot became a practice others can revisit, not a fixed program that every future resident must obey. The hearth is ready for another cook when one chooses to return.

entries.title: The Cart Beside the Road
entries.body:
Gideon Park giữ lại chiếc xe không phải vì gỗ của nó quý hơn những gì đã cháy. Ông muốn biết một phương tiện có thể trở lại hữu ích mà không trở thành vật sở hữu của người sửa nó. Rowan đề nghị kiểm tra từng bộ phận trước khi kéo xe ra đường. Việc ấy không thay thế những chiếc xe mất trong đêm tập kích; nó chỉ cho biết liệu chiếc còn lại có thể chở đồ an toàn hay không.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — a useful object can be offered back

Gideon wipes the dust from the cart handle before he asks Rowan to take it. The gesture is half habit and half apology: he has kept the broken frame under a tarp while the rest of the village decided what could be salvaged. Mira says the frame has value only if someone can safely use it, but she does not call that a reason to give it to the loudest household. Gideon wants the first repair decision recorded as a question put to the people who may depend on the road. Rowan writes that the cart is being assessed for shared use. No one signs away ownership of every tool they may later contribute.

Second road hearing — the offer is not ownership

After the repaired cart returns from its first trip, Mira asks Gideon whether the people who accepted the offer still consider it his. Gideon says he brought the old frame into the square, but that does not give him a claim over every journey it may carry. Mira remembers who first used it for medicine; another neighbor remembers the blankets tied along its side. The recollections do not agree about which trip came first, so Rowan keeps both beside the date of the repair.

They leave the cart where visitors can see it and let the next person choose whether to use it. Gideon refuses to turn the offer into a sign-up list. A person may ask for a ride without explaining why, and a person may decline to lend the cart without being called selfish. The archive records how the object became available, not who now deserves it. Its earlier use remains part of the history, while the next trip belongs to whoever agrees to make it.

entries.title: The Split Hub
entries.body:
Moay-ơ nứt chạy theo thớ, còn hai chốt sắt vẫn giữ vòng ngoài đúng vị trí. Gideon không gọi nó là một sửa chữa tạm đủ tốt: khi tải lệch sang mép bánh, vết nứt sẽ chịu thêm lực. Rowan đánh dấu chỗ yếu để người sau không kéo xe thử trước khi có chốt trục vừa kích thước.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — chalk the crack before the wheel turns

Tomas asks Gideon to mark both ends of the split hub with chalk while the wheel is still on its stand. After Rowan rotates it by hand, the line at the lower end looks wider, though the light has also shifted across the rim. They stop the wheel and make a second mark from the same angle. Gideon admits that he once heard a knock in this hub and kept using the cart because it was the only one near the shelter. The record preserves that recollection without assigning the crack to that day. The wheel stays off the road until the new pin is fitted and a separate inspection can begin.

Second road hearing — the crack gets a new inspection date

Tomas checks the wheel after the second rain. The iron ring still sits evenly against the rim, but a wet stain has made the old split difficult to see. He dries the wood with a cloth and asks Rowan to mark the crack's end again from the same side. It has not visibly advanced. Tomas writes that as one comparison under damp conditions, not as a guarantee that the wheel will stay unchanged.

Gideon wants to roll the cart immediately and is disappointed when Tomas asks him to wait until the wood is fully dry. Their disagreement is small but useful: urgency has not made the damaged section easier to judge. The new card gives the wheel another inspection date and says to stop if the ring shifts or the split lengthens. No one calls the cart unsafe forever or safe without limit. They have a repair that can be watched and a clear reason to return it to the stand.

entries.title: Mira's Dry Load
entries.body:
Mira Cole đề nghị thử chở lọ thuốc rỗng bọc vải thay vì dùng một bệnh nhân làm tải thử. Giấy liều phải nằm trong túi chống mưa và được đặt phía trên chứ không ép sát thành xe. Cô không giao cho Rowan danh sách người sẽ nhận thuốc; thứ cô cần kiểm tra là độ rung và việc giấy có còn đọc được sau chuyến đi.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — the medicine load is a route question

Mira arranges empty bottles inside a cloth wrap and asks Rowan to walk the proposed path before anyone loads medicine. The lower rut tilts the tray toward the wheel; a higher shelf keeps the bottles level but adds time and one tight turn. She asks the person carrying the kit which route they would choose, rather than deciding that speed matters most. The test uses empty glass, not a patient or a real dose. Mira writes down where the wrap was tied and which turn felt difficult to manage. A cart may carry a dry load along one path and still need a different arrangement for another trip.

Second road hearing — the medicine stays within reach

Mira tests the cloth knot with a glass bottle filled to the same level as a tonic jar. On the first run, the knot loosens where the cart bounces over the village stones. She moves the tie point farther inside the rail and asks Rowan to walk beside the wheel while she watches the load. The second run holds, though they have tested only a light parcel over a short path.

Mira leaves one small space open beside the bottle. A traveler should be able to take the medicine without unpacking the blankets or asking Gideon to move the whole load. She does not label the space with a patient's name. The card says what can be reached and how the knot was tied; it does not say who needs the jar. Gideon offers to carry the first parcel, then asks whether someone else wants the handle. Mira lets the crew decide. A practical handoff can keep help available without making the recipient visible to everyone in the square.

entries.title: Two Ruts, One Turn
entries.body:
Hai rãnh xe cũ không sâu bằng nhau. Mặt đường khô gần bậc đá nhưng đoạn thấp giữ nước và buộc người kéo phải đổi hướng sớm. Gideon ghi lại lối vòng cùng điểm quay đầu, không dùng một vệt bánh đơn lẻ để suy đoán ai đã đi qua hay thứ gì được chở. Bản đo giúp chọn đường thử, chưa xác nhận con đường có thể chịu mọi tải.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — keep the shallow turn visible on the map

The narrow track bends around a low stone where a footpath joins the road. Gideon used to cut the corner when the cart was empty. Now he walks the arc slowly with Rowan and notices that the outer wheel leaves the firm ground sooner than the inner one. They mark the shallow path and the wider detour separately. Mira asks them to keep the footpath clear for people moving between the well and shelter. The new map does not claim that every traveler can use either route in the rain. It records where a cart can turn today, so a future repair crew can ask who else needs room before widening the road.

Second road hearing — one rut changes after the storm

The east rut is shallower than it was on the day Rowan measured it. Rain filled the low point, and a neighbor packed the edge with broken brick before the cart came back. Gideon recognizes the curve but not the exact patch of ground. Rowan repeats the test with the empty cart and draws a new chalk line beside the old one. The wheel follows a slightly wider turn.

Tomas asks them to keep the earlier mark instead of replacing it. The first line belongs to dry ground; the second belongs to a patched lane after rain. Both can help another driver understand why the cart was guided around the stone step. Neither line is a permanent road instruction. A child points out that the turning space narrows when a water barrel is left near the wall. Gideon moves the barrel for this test and records its temporary location. The page now describes a route with weather, patching and nearby objects attached, not a universal radius for every cart in Ashfall.

entries.title: The Goblin Under the Cart
entries.body:
Ash Goblin đã kéo một dải sắt cong ra khỏi đường thử và dùng gầm xe làm chỗ ẩn. Rowan đợi nó rời khỏi khung gỗ trước khi phản công, để cú đánh không làm nứt thêm bánh xe. Dải sắt thu hồi được nhưng biến dạng; nó có thể làm vật liệu rèn sau khi được đo lại, song bản thân nó không chứng minh ai đã bỏ xe tại đây.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — clear the road after the fight as well

The Ash Goblin retreats beneath the cart shed, and Rowan draws it away before striking. Gideon stays beside the frame, ready to pull the tarp free if a loose board falls. After the fight, they find one bent strip of iron under the wheel and a smear of mud on the ground; neither shows whether the creature brought the strip there or moved it while hiding. Rowan stores the iron with the salvage but leaves the mud undisturbed until Gideon has checked the wheel stand. The encounter ends when the path is safe to approach, not when the last hit lands. The repair notes separate what the team recovered from what it only noticed.

Second road hearing — the goblin left, and the road remains

Rowan returns to the cart after the Ash Goblin has fled from beneath it. The axle is exposed, and no new mark crosses the wheel's cracked section. Gideon asks whether the creature had been trying to steal the iron. Rowan cannot tell. A few loose scraps have moved, but the fight and the earlier salvage work happened in the same small space. He records where the goblin appeared and what remained visible after the encounter, then keeps motive out of the note.

Mira finds a clean path to the medicine parcel and moves it before the repair begins. The cleared area makes the next inspection possible; it does not explain why the creature chose that hiding place. Gideon says the lane feels less threatening now that the cart can move, but he does not ask Rowan to turn that feeling into a report about everyone else's safety. The archive preserves one resolved encounter beside several unanswered questions. Clearing the immediate obstacle lets the group resume their work without pretending the whole road has been understood.

entries.title: Salvage Is Not a Part Yet
entries.body:
Trong đống vật liệu có một đoạn sắt gần như thẳng và hai nan gỗ nứt ở đầu. Rowan chỉ giữ đoạn sắt để Tomas kiểm tra; vật liệu trông còn nguyên không có nghĩa là đã chịu được lực của xe. Gideon cấp lại phần phế liệu cho người sửa thay vì tính nó là hàng chung, để nguồn gốc và giới hạn sử dụng không bị bỏ khỏi bản ghi.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — let the owner review the scrap pile

Gideon places the straight iron on a board beside the two cracked spokes and asks Rowan not to carry anything away yet. He recognizes the pale stripe on one piece as a mark he used when the cart was repaired years ago, but the stripe could have been copied from another workshop. Tomas takes measurements in Gideon's presence and gives each item back before deciding what can be used. The surviving pieces belong to the cart's repair history even if none is safe to install. They record which material was inspected and which was rejected. Salvage becomes a part only after someone checks its condition and the person who brought it in agrees to the proposed use.

Second road hearing — keep the iron separate from the inventory

The two salvaged pieces are placed beside Tomas's bench after the axle pin is installed. One length has a bright edge where the smith cut it; the other still carries soot from the old cart. Gideon asks if both should be entered as replacement parts. Tomas says only the fitted pin has been tried under the wheel. The remaining length has not passed a matching check, and the old spoke was used as a gauge rather than installed as timber.

Rowan makes three labels: fitted pin, untested iron and measuring spoke. The labels look fussy until a volunteer reaches for the wrong length to repair a handcart. Tomas shows them the difference and lets the volunteer decide whether to keep the material for a later job. No one marks the untested iron as wasted, but no one promises it will fit another axle. Salvage can remain useful without being counted as a functioning part. Gideon keeps the box at the workshop, where another repairer can ask before taking anything.

entries.title: A Turning Measure
entries.body:
Gideon phân biệt điều ông nhớ về chiếc xe cũ với điều Rowan vừa đo trên con đường hiện tại. Bán kính quay phải được kiểm tra ở tốc độ đi bộ, với thùng nhẹ và người kéo có thể dừng ngay. Dấu bánh ngoài sẽ cho biết xe cần thêm chỗ trống; nó không cho phép đội sửa tự mở rộng đường qua phần đất của hộ khác.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — repeat the turn after the road dries

Gideon remembers steering this frame through the eastern lane before the raid, when the path was covered in frost. Rowan's trial takes place on dry earth, so they mark a second pass for the next morning if the ground remains firm. The turning arc can change when mud softens the shoulder or when a wheel slips. They set a walking pace and keep the cart empty; a fast turn could hide the moment the hub shifts. Gideon watches the outer wheel while Rowan guides the handle, then they trade places. Their impressions differ at the tight corner. Both are written down so a later test can repeat the same roles or deliberately compare them.

Second road hearing — the turning line needs its load condition

Rowan repeats the turning test with a cloth bundle weighing roughly as much as the medicine crate. The outer wheel reaches farther than it did with the empty frame. A heavier load shifts the cart's balance before the handle reaches the painted stone. Gideon remembers that the old cart once turned in the lane while full of firewood, but he cannot remember which bundles were aboard or how the ground had dried.

They draw two arcs: one from the empty trial and one from the light parcel. The second line is not a prediction for a full cart. Tomas asks that the card state the load and surface beside each mark, since a future worker could otherwise mistake the pair for an allowance. Gideon wants one easy circle that anyone can follow; Rowan explains that a circle without conditions would hide the part they actually learned. They keep the test simple enough to repeat and leave the larger-load question open for a day when the road crew can choose to try it safely.

entries.title: Tomas's Shoulder Pin
entries.body:
Tomas Reed đo vai chặn theo độ dày vòng sắt và đường nứt mà Rowan ghi lại. Ông từ chối khoan thêm một lỗ để buộc bánh vào vị trí: lỗ mới sẽ cắt ngang phần gỗ còn chịu tải. Công thức chốt dùng phần sắt và một nan thẳng làm cữ. Bản mẫu ở lò giúp các thợ khác rèn lại kích thước, nhưng không thay thế việc kiểm tra chiếc xe đã sửa.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — the shoulder pin follows the tested edge

Tomas sets the old pin beside the cracked hub and measures the shoulder twice before heating a new blank. He explains that adding another bore would remove wood from the narrowest part of the rim. Gideon wants the repair finished before the next supply run, but agrees to wait while Tomas cuts the pin to the recorded fit. The forge card names the iron source, jaw setting and bench used, then leaves a blank for the next inspection. Rowan watches Tomas reject one rough blank with a shallow seam. It could be straightened, but the seam would sit where the cart carries its turning force. Speed cannot make an uncertain piece part of the repair.

Second road hearing — the shoulder is a stop, not decoration

Tomas lays the axle pin against the wheel and lets Rowan feel the raised shoulder with one finger. The shoulder prevents the pin from sliding inward when the wheel turns, while the outside end remains accessible for inspection. A hurried repair could make the rod look secure from the front and still leave it free to travel through the hub. Tomas draws the section twice because the first sketch hid the lip beneath the iron ring.

Gideon asks whether the shape can be copied for a different cart. Tomas says the drawing gives another smith a place to start, but the hub width, wood condition and load must be checked first. He writes down the material and the dimensions of this pin, then leaves blank space for any later replacement. Rowan understands why Tomas avoids calling the sketch a pattern. The part's safety comes from its fit and its inspection, not from being named after the person who made it. Gideon adds the date he received the pin so its custody can be followed without implying that he owns every future repair.

entries.title: The Spoke Used as a Gauge
entries.body:
Nan gỗ chỉ dùng làm cữ giữ khoảng cách trong lúc rèn, không được lắp vào xe thay cho một phần chịu tải. Tomas đặt thước kim loại bên cạnh để Rowan có thể lặp lại số đo mà không phụ thuộc vào độ ẩm của gỗ. Việc tách cữ khỏi phụ tùng giúp người sửa sau không nhầm một món hỗ trợ chế tác với bộ phận có thể chở hàng trên đường.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — the spoke measures distance, then goes back to storage

Rowan holds the cracked spoke against the metal rule while Tomas checks the gap at the hub. They mark the measurement on a card rather than carving it into the wood, which is already split near its head. The spoke returns to Gideon's salvage tray once the forge has its note. Mira asks that the tray stay apart from usable repair stock so someone searching for parts does not mistake the broken wood for a ready replacement. It remains a gauge sample, not a component. The card adds where the rule touched and which end of the spoke faced the rim. A future maker can use a new piece to repeat the measurement without forcing this one back into the cart.

Second road hearing — a gauge can fail in a useful way

The straight spoke rests across the wheel rim while Tomas checks the gap at three points. At the top, it touches both edges. Near the lower nail, a warped section leaves a thin line of daylight. Rowan had first thought the spoke was straight enough to use as a replacement; Tomas asks him to turn it end for end and repeat the comparison. The gap changes sides, revealing a bend too slight to notice by eye.

Gideon keeps the spoke on the bench rather than throwing it away. It still shows where the rim narrows, provided the card mentions its bend and the direction used during measurement. They do not use it to support the cart. Mira says the test gave them a better question for the next board, not a perfect measuring tool. Rowan records the result as a rejected part that remains a rough reference. The note will help another worker avoid mistaking a convenient straight edge for a verified standard.

entries.title: Ashfall Axle Pin
entries.body:
Chốt vai trục được rèn từ đoạn sắt cứu ở Ashfall. Nan gỗ dùng làm cữ được giữ riêng và không bị tiêu hao như thể nó là sắt. Tomas kiểm tra vai chặn bằng thước trước khi đưa chốt cho Rowan. Độ khớp tại lò mới chỉ xác nhận kích thước ban đầu; chiếc xe cần được lắp thử và xoay không tải để phát hiện ma sát.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — record the pin's cooling place

Tomas lets the forged pin cool on a marked stone separate from the scraps waiting for inspection. He measures its shoulder after cooling and again after it has rested through one forge watch. The second mark is close, but he keeps both readings rather than calling the first an error. The pin is stamped with the date and a tiny workshop sign that identifies its maker, not the cart's owner. Gideon asks to keep the sign small enough that it will not catch the cloth wrap. The tool card travels with the part until installation. If the pin later needs removal, another smith can see what was fitted and how Tomas checked it.

Second road hearing — the forge is not where the trial ends

The pin leaves the forge cool enough to handle, and Tomas checks its shoulder against the drawing. He finds no visible burr, but he does not ask Gideon to install it while the metal is still warm. The cart has been waiting outside; the crew would like to finish before dark. Tomas closes the tongs and says the bench check has one purpose: confirm that the part resembles its dimensions before it meets a wooden hub.

After the pin cools, the shoulder slips into the gauge without scraping. Tomas signs for the forging step only. Rowan adds a separate line for installation, which will be checked under the wheel. The distinction matters because a clean part can still be wrong for a damaged hub. Gideon accepts the delay when Mira offers to carry the medicine parcel by hand. The cart will move later, after the fit is known. No one treats the completed craft action as proof that the vehicle is ready for the road.

entries.title: The Part Returns with Its Measure
entries.body:
Rowan mang về chốt đã rèn cùng phép đo và lưu ý từ Tomas. Gideon hỏi về chiếc nan làm cữ trước khi chạm vào xe, vì một bộ phận chưa thử rất dễ bị coi nhầm là phụ tùng dự phòng. Hai người thống nhất lắp chốt, xoay bánh khi xe còn kê cao, rồi mới thử tải nhẹ. Không có bước nào trong quy trình coi sự vội vàng là bằng chứng của độ bền.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — bring back the measuring rule too

Rowan returns the pin, the calibration card and Tomas's metal rule together. Gideon checks the card before touching the cart and notices that the spoke used as a gauge is not in the bundle. Rowan retrieves it from the forge tray and marks it “broken sample” so it cannot be mistaken for spare stock. Tomas asks for the rule back after installation, because the next inspection must use the same tool or record that a different one was used. The handoff includes more than the finished part: it preserves the path by which the part was measured. Gideon files the card with the cart papers instead of leaving it loose on the workbench.

Second road hearing — return the sample before lending the tool

Gideon brings the measuring spoke back to Tomas after the turn test. A strip of chalk on the wood shows which edge was placed against the rim, so Tomas can repeat the check without guessing. He wipes the mark away only after Rowan copies its orientation into the ledger. The spoken explanation would probably survive between the two of them; the note is for the next repairer, who may arrive after both have left.

Mira asks whether she can borrow the gauge for the shelter cart. Tomas agrees, then writes down when it leaves the bench and leaves an empty line for its return. He does not ask her to provide a reason or a household name. The tool is useful because it travels, but its measurement is only as clear as the conditions carried with it. Rowan adds that the spoke remains a reference and must not be installed. The handoff gives Mira access without erasing Tomas's responsibility to explain what the instrument can and cannot show.

entries.title: A Wheel That Turns by Hand
entries.body:
Chốt được lắp vào moay-ơ và vai chặn nằm ngoài vòng sắt. Rowan xoay bánh đủ một vòng khi thân xe còn kê cao; bánh không cạ vào càng và vết nứt không mở rộng trong phép thử chậm này. Gideon đánh dấu bộ phận đã lắp nhưng chưa gọi xe an toàn cho hàng. Thử không tải chỉ mở bước kiểm tra tiếp theo.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — turn the wheel without a crowd around it

Before the wheel is lowered, Gideon asks the onlookers to step back from the stand. Rowan seats the pin, checks that the shoulder rests outside the iron ring and turns the wheel slowly by hand. It completes one circle without scraping. Tomas watches the mark on the hub, while Mira checks that no cloth has caught near the spokes. The test is quiet and brief. Gideon wants to celebrate by pushing the cart at once; Rowan points to the next inspection card. The repair is now installed, but a wheel that turns freely in the air has not yet carried anyone or anything on the road.

Second road hearing — installation leaves the old hole visible

Once the pin is fitted, Tomas shines a small lantern through the hub to inspect its path. The new shoulder rests outside the iron ring, while a dark stain marks the older place where the wood was split. Gideon wants a fresh coat of paint to make the repair look finished. Mira asks them to wait until the wheel has turned through its hand test; paint could cover a new scrape before anyone notices it.

They rotate the empty wheel slowly. The pin stays in place, and the ring does not catch. Rowan marks the test complete beside the date, then adds a reminder to inspect the same point after the cart travels over the repaired lane. Gideon decides to leave the old hole visible under a clear coat. It helps distinguish the new fitting from the damage that came before. A repair can be neat without hiding its history, and a visible mark can guide future inspection without being treated as evidence of who caused the break.

entries.title: Empty Cart Trial
entries.body:
Xe rỗng lăn được trên đoạn bằng đã chọn. Rowan dừng trước rãnh sâu thay vì dùng đà để vượt qua một chỗ chưa đo. Gideon kiểm tra chốt sau khi dừng, còn Mira sẽ xem vị trí đặt hàng nhẹ. Kết quả chỉ áp dụng cho đoạn ngắn, mặt đường khô và xe không tải; mưa hoặc trọng lượng lệch có thể làm đổi hành vi của bánh.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — stop at the marker, not at the rut

The empty cart rolls along the chalked strip and stops at the short marker Rowan placed before the deep rut. Gideon checks the pin, then walks back to the start to see whether the wheel left a new track. They find one shallow groove at the turn and no visible change at the hub. Mira asks that the cart remain empty until she has reviewed how a wrapped bottle sits in its tray. No one asks a villager to ride along as proof. The trial establishes that this frame moved across a short dry path under hand control. A different surface, a slope or a full load requires a different review.

Second road hearing — the empty run has a clear boundary

The first full turn takes place on a dry, flat stretch. Rowan walks beside the right wheel and calls out when the iron ring passes the painted line. The cart rolls without wobbling, but the test stops before the lane's shallow rut. Gideon says it felt steady. Tomas writes that the wheel remained aligned during one empty run on level ground, which is more precise and less impressive than declaring the repair complete under every condition.

They place a low cone at the end of the trial so no one mistakes the boundary for a marker to cross. Mira asks that the medicine stay off the cart until the next test, since she wants a separate note for a carried load. The crew can now decide whether to repeat the run or wait for a second pair of hands. No one is required to volunteer for the next attempt. Rowan records the people who agreed to assist but leaves the public copy without names. The lane is ready for another chosen trial, not yet cleared for every kind of trip.

entries.title: The Cloth Knot Test
entries.body:
Mira chọn một nút vải có thể tháo để đánh dấu vị trí đặt túi thuốc. Nút không mang tên người bệnh và không biến chiếc xe thành quầy phát thuốc cố định. Cô muốn thử một lọ rỗng trước, lắc xe ở tốc độ đi bộ rồi kiểm tra nắp và tờ liều. Hàng thật chỉ được đặt lên xe khi người phụ trách thuốc đồng ý với cách buộc.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — tie the marker where a carrier can reach it

Mira ties the cloth knot low on the inside rail, where a person standing beside the cart can loosen it without lifting the tray. The knot marks the test position for an empty medicine wrap; it does not reserve that place for a named patient. Rowan walks the cart over the short dry strip and the bottles remain still. They do not fill the bottles with water to imitate a dose, because a liquid load would shift differently and could spill. Mira adds a second position for a soft blanket bundle and leaves the choice of which arrangement to use to the carrier. The marker is an invitation to check, not a label for a person.

Second road hearing — a knot is part of the route

Mira asks a neighbor who has never tied a cart parcel to try the cloth knot from the illustrated card. The neighbor places the jar near the outer rail, where it knocks against a spoke when the cart starts. They stop before the glass breaks. Rowan moves the strap inward and lets the neighbor try again without taking over the work. This time, the jar stays still through the small turn.

The card gains a picture of the knot from the hand that made it, with a note that the parcel should sit inside the wheel line. Mira asks whether the neighbor wants their name shown. They decline, so the public record says only that a first-time user found the drawing unclear. The change improves the instruction without making a person into an example against their wishes. Gideon suggests adding a second knot for heavier cargo. Tomas says that would need another test with a load chosen by the people who will carry it. They keep the current card narrow enough to remain true.

entries.title: Two Ways to Keep a Cart Moving
entries.body:
Một chiếc xe chung có thể chở nhiều loại hàng nhưng cần quy ước bàn giao rõ và chỗ để không chắn lối. Bộ sửa nhỏ giúp các hộ tự siết chốt khi bánh lỏng, song không thay được xe tải hay người kéo. Gideon không xem một cách là mặc nhiên công bằng hơn; Rowan phải chọn thứ có thể kiểm tra trong điều kiện Ashfall hiện có. Người dùng sau này vẫn có quyền đổi lịch hoặc từ chối nhận vật liệu.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — compare the upkeep each choice asks of people

At the shelter table, Gideon lays out a board for a shared parking bay and a small case for household repair kits. The shared cart needs a schedule, a clear return point and someone able to inspect the pin. The kits need a stock count, a place to ask questions and a rule for replacing parts that wear out. Mira asks who would be able to refuse each arrangement without losing access to the road. Rowan records the answers separately rather than ranking the two options as generous or selfish. The choice decides which upkeep the village will try first. It does not make every household responsible for pulling a cart or keeping a forge tool.

Second road hearing — a shared cart and a home kit solve different waits

The village holds a short meeting at the bay. One household prefers a cart they can borrow without buying a replacement wheel; another already has a small handcart and would rather keep a pin and gauge at home. Gideon lays out both proposals without asking either family to defend its budget. The shared option needs a visible return time and room to turn. The household option needs clear instructions and a way to request help when the repair exceeds a person's tools.

Rowan writes the practical obligations beside each choice, not above it as a ranking. A cart schedule can fail if nobody wants the next shift; a kit can sit unused if its parts are difficult to identify. Mira offers to keep the drawing at the medicine table, where people may read it without taking a kit. Gideon agrees that the next arrangement should be reviewed after it has been used. The choice flag records what Rowan helped organize today. It does not decide which method every Ashfall household must prefer.

entries.title: The Shared Bay
entries.body:
Chỗ đỗ chung được đặt lệch khỏi cửa hầm và đường đến giếng. Rowan thử lối quay đầu với xe rỗng rồi để hai đầu dây bàn giao dễ nhận ra. Vị trí này không dành riêng cho một hộ; người kéo có thể đưa xe đi nếu cần sơ tán hoặc chở thuốc. Gideon vẫn giữ quyền sửa lại vạch khi người đi đường thấy nó chắn lối.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — leave a clear line from the bay to the well

Gideon marks the proposed bay outside the shelter door, then Mira asks him to move it away from the shortest path to the well. A cart parked there would force people carrying water to step into the wheel rut. Rowan walks the new route with an empty basket and checks that the handle can turn without striking the stone post. They keep a chalk space at the entrance for temporary unloading, but do not call it a permanent storage place. The shared bay works only if its use does not block another daily route. The map shows the bay, the well path and the turning arc on separate lines so later residents can revise the position.

Second road hearing — keep the turning space empty for a reason

The bay stays clear for most of the morning, then a sack of kindling appears beside the wall. Its owner set it there to keep the doorway open and did not know the cart needed a wider turn. Gideon moves the sack with permission and asks whether another storage spot is available. The owner chooses one near the shelter steps. They make the change together rather than writing the name on a warning card.

Rowan measures the empty arc once more, this time with the new stack of crates near the lane. The cart still turns, but its handle passes close to the wall. They shift the crates half a pace and draw a chalk boundary that can be rubbed away if the bay changes. A permanent painted box would look official even after the route changed. The shared space works today because neighbors can ask about stored objects and move them by agreement. The ledger records the clearance and the conditions around it, not a claim that the village has reserved this ground forever.

entries.title: The Turning Arc
entries.body:
Vệt quay cho thấy bánh ngoài cùng cần một khoảng trống vừa hơn chiều ngang xe. Rowan ghi điều kiện mặt đất khô và tốc độ đi bộ ngay cạnh vạch, vì một dấu không có bối cảnh dễ bị dùng sai ở lối hẹp khác. Nếu nền lún hoặc xe mang hàng cao, bán kính quay thay đổi; người kéo có thể dừng và chọn lối khác thay vì ép qua.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — the chalk arc can be erased and drawn again

After the first turn, rain breaks the chalk line at the outer wheel. Rowan redraws it from the same starting mark and writes that the second trial followed a shower, while the ground still looked firm. Gideon notices the wheel has cut a little deeper near the gate. They do not average the first and second arcs; one was traced on dry soil and one on damp soil. A shared bay needs space for the cart as it turns, but its boundary should not claim more ground than the village can keep clear. The chalk can be moved after another trial. The record leaves a note for whoever has permission to change it.

Second road hearing — count the turns that stop early

The cart makes one complete turn before lunch. On the second attempt, a loose stone rolls beneath the outer wheel and Gideon stops before the handle reaches the chalk arc. Rowan asks whether to record that as a failed turn. Tomas says it is a stop caused by the surface; it is useful to keep because future users should know why the trial ended. They remove the stone and do not repeat the attempt until someone checks the wheel again.

The report now includes one completed turn and one interrupted run, with different marks beside them. The difference prevents a neat total from hiding the caution that changed the work. A visitor offers to smooth the whole lane, but the group has not agreed on how much ground belongs to the bay. Gideon thanks them and asks for a smaller patch near the wheel track instead. The shared cart remains available under the posted conditions. The space for an early stop stays part of the instructions, because safety work is also the ability to end a trial before a small warning becomes a larger repair.

entries.title: A Cart Shared by Choice
entries.body:
Lịch dùng xe ghi thời điểm nhận và trả, không phân công người kéo theo tên hộ. Người mượn tự chọn nhận việc, báo hỏng và đề nghị đổi đường. Gideon chịu trách nhiệm kiểm tra chốt định kỳ cùng người sử dụng đầu tiên, nhưng lịch không biến một lời đồng ý hôm nay thành nghĩa vụ cho tuần sau. Chỗ đỗ và vệt quay vẫn có thể được thay đổi khi lối đi cần rộng hơn.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — a missed handoff does not name a culprit

The first shared schedule leaves a gap at dusk when the gate watch changes. The cart stands at the bay after the expected return time, so Gideon asks if anyone knows who last used it. Rowan adds an “unconfirmed return” mark and checks the wheel instead of copying a name from the duty board. The cart is intact, and a neighbor brings it back after the well path clears. They add a wider handoff window for the next week. The incident shows that the schedule needs room for delays; it does not prove anyone broke an agreement. Users can report a change of plan without defending themselves before taking the cart again.

Second road hearing — the return board records an object, not a person

The first cart user writes “back at the bay” on the slate and wipes the chalk away after unloading. Another resident asks whether the schedule should include the borrower's name so the next user can ask questions. Gideon says the cart can carry a contact token if someone volunteers to be reached, but a name is not a condition of borrowing. They leave a small blank for a return time and an optional note about the lane.

Mira adds a line for damage or a changed strap. She does not add “reason for trip.” The next person can check the wheel, read the load card and decide whether the cart meets their own needs. Rowan records that the schedule was used twice and does not estimate how many households now depend on it. A shared object needs a reliable handoff, not a census. If the bay becomes inconvenient, its users can request a change. Gideon agrees to ask again after several trips instead of treating the first week as a final policy.

entries.title: Portable Repair Kits
entries.body:
Các bộ nhỏ chứa cữ đo, một chốt dự phòng và tờ chỉ dẫn kiểm tra độ cạ. Chúng không gồm bánh xe hoàn chỉnh và không thể sửa mọi dạng gãy. Gideon muốn mỗi hộ quyết định có nhận bộ hay không; Rowan đánh dấu bộ chưa thử bằng dây màu thay vì tên người. Việc phân tán dụng cụ giảm nhu cầu chờ xe chung nhưng cũng khiến mỗi người phải tự giữ vật liệu an toàn.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — count each kit before handing it over

Mira lays one repair kit on a dry cloth: a measuring gauge, a checked pin and a short instruction card. The kit cannot straighten a bent frame or replace Tomas's forge work. Gideon asks that the parts be counted at return, since a missing pin may mean it was used to keep a wheel from failing on the road. The card says where to bring a damaged tool and how to request a replacement without explaining a household's need in public. Mira tracks stock by item and condition, not by the names of people who borrowed it. A small case can make one repair easier, but it is not an emergency service for every broken cart.

Second road hearing — a kit should explain what is missing

The repair kits arrive with one shoulder pin, a measuring card and a cloth envelope for loose fasteners. Mira notices that the first envelope has no label for an empty compartment. A missing piece might mean it was used, lost or never included. She and Tomas add three check boxes on the card and ask each household which format is easier to read. One person wants words; another circles small drawings.

Gideon offers to deliver the kits, but two neighbors prefer to collect theirs when they visit the square. Nobody has to sign for receiving one. The inventory can track how many kits were assembled without naming who took them. Rowan suggests adding an optional way to ask for another pin. Tomas writes the forge location beside it, so the instructions do not promise that a replacement is always on hand. The kit is an invitation to try a small repair, not a transfer of responsibility for every broken cart onto each household. Help remains part of the plan.

entries.title: A Test on the Stand
entries.body:
Mira giữ bánh xe trên giá thử, tránh biến một hộ đang dùng xe thành đối tượng thử nghiệm. Chốt lắp được và bánh quay đều khi siết đúng lực, nhưng phép thử không bao phủ khung cong hay tải nặng. Rowan thêm hướng dẫn dừng nếu tiếng cạ trở lại hoặc vòng sắt dịch chuyển. Bộ sửa là dụng cụ bảo dưỡng cơ bản, không thay công việc của thợ rèn.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — test the pin on the stand again after travel

The kit returns from the far lane with the pin still in its wrap. Mira places the matching wheel on the stand and asks Rowan to compare it with the original fit mark. The pin seats cleanly, but the stand holds the wheel at a different angle than the cart frame did. Gideon suggests adding that limitation to the instruction card. They run the check once more with the stand level and record both setups. The trial helps a household notice a loose pin before a trip; it cannot certify a repaired cart or teach every person to judge a cracked hub. People can bring the part back to the forge when the check raises a question.

Second road hearing — two stands reveal two different problems

Mira tests a loose wheel on the wooden stand, while Tomas repeats the same hand turn on the iron stand at the forge. The wood frame flexes slightly when the pin is pushed sideways; the iron frame holds still. Neither result means that one stand is useless. The household kit is meant to help someone notice a loose fitting before a cart is loaded, not to imitate every force it may meet on the road.

They add a warning to stop if the stand itself shifts. One household asks to keep the kit near the door; another puts it above a dry shelf. The archive does not choose a storage place for them. Rowan records which stand was used in each trial so a later reader can compare results without treating them as identical. Tomas asks for a road test only if the cart owner agrees and a second person can walk beside the wheel. A repair instruction should make stopping ordinary, not embarrassing.

entries.title: Repair Stock with an Opt-In
entries.body:
Mira đặt hướng dẫn ở bàn thuốc cùng số chốt còn lại, để người cần tự hỏi và lấy bộ sửa. Cô không ghi ai đã nhận để kiểm đếm mức độ khó khăn; chỉ vật liệu tồn kho được theo dõi. Gideon giữ lại cữ để rèn thêm khi có sắt tốt. Những hộ không muốn tự sửa vẫn có thể nhờ thợ hoặc mượn xe chung khi lối đi và lịch cho phép.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — stock numbers can change without a borrower list

Gideon counts two pins in the case and writes the total on the shelf card. One kit is out for inspection, but Mira leaves its borrower field blank because the village only needs to know that the tool has not returned yet. When the kit comes back, the count changes and the shelf card is updated. A private request can be made at the medicine table if the person wants help finding a part. Nobody has to explain their route or cargo to receive a measuring tool. The stock record answers how many parts remain; it does not describe who owns a cart or who has asked for assistance.

Second road hearing — asking for help is part of the kit

Mira finds a note tucked beside the measuring card: “I can fit the pin, but I cannot tell if the hub is splitting.” She recognizes the question as a reason to stop and asks the writer whether it may be copied into the public instructions. The writer agrees without signing their name. Tomas adds a simple check: if a crack continues past the iron ring, do not load the wheel; bring the cart to the forge or ask a repairer to inspect it.

Gideon wants to know which household wrote the note so he can check on them. Mira explains that the cart owner can contact him directly if they want help. The public record can answer the repair question without exposing the person who asked it. Rowan leaves the name field blank and adds the date the instruction changed. The household kit now has a route back to skilled support, rather than a promise that everyone must become their own mechanic. A tool is useful when it also shows where its limits begin.

entries.title: Afterword: The Road Stays Open
entries.body:
Ashfall hiện có một chiếc xe đã sửa, một đường thử ngắn và một quy trình lắp chốt có thể lặp lại. Lựa chọn của Rowan quyết định làng ưu tiên xe chung với lịch bàn giao hay các bộ sửa tự nguyện cho từng hộ. Cả hai cách vẫn giữ quyền dừng khi tải hoặc mặt đường vượt quá điều đã thử. Gideon cất dụng cụ trong tầm với của người sửa tiếp theo; chiếc xe không trở thành biểu tượng rằng làng đã hồi phục hoàn toàn.

Supplemental Ashfall cart note —Supplemental Ashfall cart note — keep the road open to a different repair

At the end of the route, Gideon takes the cart down the lane without cargo and stops at the gate to listen for the old knock. It does not return on this pass. He leaves the pin card beside the tool case, not attached permanently to the frame, so a future repairer can replace it and keep the earlier record. Rowan writes that the village chose a shared bay or voluntary kits for the current season. Neither choice prevents residents from asking to try the other later. The road has one repaired cart, a tested short path and a way to request another inspection. Its next use belongs to the people who decide to travel it.

Second road hearing — leave a place for the next repairer

At the end of the month, the shared cart has made several short trips and spent one week under cover while a new scrape was inspected. The home kits have been borrowed for two loose pins; one came back with a note asking for a smaller measuring card. Gideon expected the village to settle on one arrangement. Instead, both are still being used in different places, and each has acquired a small revision.

Rowan makes two copies of the archive: one stays with Tomas's workshop, the other with the bay schedule. They include the conditions of the trials, the names of those who chose to sign, and blank space for someone to disagree or add a date. Mira says a record should be easy to correct before it becomes a rule. Gideon puts the cart key back on its hook without locking the shed. The road remains open for another journey, but nobody claims that a repaired wheel can promise the future will be smooth. The next repairer will have a place to begin and permission to change the page.

entries.title: A Book with an Unfinished Margin
entries.body:
Tomas does not call the blank edge of the book an omission. His first master drew a narrow line beside each pattern, a place to record where the piece was used and what changed before the repair held. Later copies removed the line to make their diagrams easier to reproduce. The drawings became tidy; the weather, wear and local material disappeared. Tomas wants the margin restored without turning it into another rule that every maker must obey. Rowan agrees to carry the book through several regions, test an adjustable gauge and write down where that gauge itself falls short.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — the margin belongs to the next repairer

Tomas finds a faint line beneath the first master's old pencil rule. It is not a measurement; it is the pressure mark left by a page that once covered the margin. He asks Rowan to hold the lamp while he compares the bound copy with a loose leaf from the same workshop. The leaf carries a note about a gate hinge after rain. That small addition explains why the original book left room beside each pattern. Tomas had thought the blank was a flaw in the copy. He now writes the two versions side by side and lets the reader see how a working page became a clean diagram.

entries.title: Notches Removed from the Master Gauge
entries.body:
The brass gauge has three movable pins and a fourth notch cut directly into its handle. The cut is cleaner than the dents around it, so it was made later, but no date survives. A fixed notch is useful when many identical pieces are made under known conditions. It becomes risky when copied onto a wheel swollen by rain or a hinge forged from a different batch of iron. Rowan records the notch as a later alteration, not as proof that someone intended to force every repair into one size.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — a removed notch leaves a readable scar

Tomas rubs chalk across the gauge handle, then wipes only the raised surface. The fourth notch takes a thin white line that the other three do not. He does not deepen it to make the old mark easier to see. Rowan traces its current width on a separate card and records that the tool has been filed since the first pattern was drawn. The pins still move, but the scar cannot say who moved them or why. Tomas decides the atlas should show both the adjustable jaws and the fixed mark, with a reminder to check the tool against a known plate before using either as a reference.

entries.title: One Cart Is One Measurement
entries.body:
Gideon's cart uses the Ashfall Axle Pin forged for its cracked hub. The old drawing shows a wider rim and a straight beam where the repaired cart now carries a slight bend. The pin works for the current wheel under an empty-cart trial on dry ground. It is not a universal pattern for carts with swollen spokes or uneven loads. Gideon asks Rowan to preserve the successful measurement with its conditions. If someone copies only the pin's length, the copy may seem exact while leaving out why that length was chosen.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — listen again after the cart returns

Gideon rolls the empty cart over the same dry strip and stops where the left wheel first caught a pebble. The new axle pin turns without a knock, but the repaired hub carries a faint wobble that Rowan had not noticed while the cart stood still. They mark the strip and repeat the pass once, then stop rather than adding cargo to a repair that has not been inspected under load. Gideon says the sound is different from the old crack. Tomas records that as the driver's observation, not as proof the hub is sound. The gauge describes one contact surface; the cart still needs its own repair check.

entries.title: A Repair Note Should Name Its Conditions
entries.body:
Gideon's old notes use 'strong enough' beside several braces. He remembers one holding a roof beam for an afternoon but cannot say whether it stayed safe after rain softened the wall. The phrase records a judgment without its boundary. On Rowan's page he describes what was present: a dry cart, no cargo and two people watching the wheel during a short roll. He does not erase the earlier wording. A reader should see what Gideon knew then and what he would ask the next repairer to test now.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — write the load before calling a brace tested

Gideon brings the old roof note to the stand and points to the phrase “strong enough.” He had written it after the brace held through an afternoon of light rain, but before the roof tiles were set back in place. He remembers the relief of seeing the beam stop moving. Rowan asks whether the phrase can remain if its conditions travel with it. Gideon adds the empty beam weight, the rain and the unfinished roof, then leaves the later load blank. The repairer's judgment is still part of the history. It simply cannot promise what was never tried.

entries.title: Windglass Reed as Packing, Not Structure
entries.body:
The harvested reed can wrap around a loose metal jaw and keep grit from lodging between the gauge and a surface. Its fibers bend with the grain but split under crosswise pressure. Tomas refuses to call it a substitute for iron. Rowan records the bed, harvest day and stem condition, then keeps one stalk whole for another maker to compare. Packing can make a tool easier to use without making it stronger. The distinction prevents the word 'reinforced' from hiding which material bears the actual force.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — replace the reed before grit packs beneath it

A short length of Windglass Reed has flattened where the gauge jaw pressed against the wheel rim. Rowan loosens the pin and finds a few grains caught under the strip. Tomas replaces the packing, puts the used reed in a marked tray and checks the jaw on the clean bench plate again. The tool feels tighter, but the change might come from the new strip or the cleaning. He records both actions before the next measurement. Mara says the spent reed can return to the garden compost only after the metal dust is removed. A soft spacer has a useful life and a disposal path; neither belongs in the structural specification.

entries.title: Saltspool Oil and a Narrow Claim
entries.body:
Rowan catches one Saltspool Skate at the sheltered pool. It leaves an oily trace on the cloth, and Tomas proposes testing a little on scrap iron. Neither observation establishes how the fish population changes through a season or whether the oil prevents corrosion in every climate. The catch record names the pool and day so the comparison can be repeated. Talia will test treated and untreated scraps side by side. Until then the oil is a candidate hinge treatment, not a recommendation for tools used near food or drinking water.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — the fish oil stays away from shared utensils

Tomas asks the cook for a clean cloth and a small covered dish before Rowan opens the Saltspool Skate sample. The oil is measured with a tool kept for workshop trials, not the kitchen ladle. After the scrap-iron test, the cloth and dish are labeled for disposal so no one mistakes a craft material for food. Rowan writes the bait, catch place and amount used, then seals the remainder. The procedure makes the trial easier to repeat without implying that oil from every catch behaves alike. If another sample is taken, its container starts clean and receives its own date.

entries.title: Two Scraps, One Matched Trial
entries.body:
Talia compares a treated scrap with an untreated one using water from the same marked cup. She labels both before they enter the basin because a later observer must know which surface received fish oil. The test lasts one watch, not a season. Temperature, flow and the cup's source remain beside the result. If one scrap changes less, that difference may justify another test; it will not identify the chemistry of every channel or certify metal for food service. A useful trial is allowed to produce a small answer.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — name the two scraps before the next watch

Talia asks Rowan to engrave a small A on the treated scrap and a B on its untreated mate. The labels are shallow enough not to change the exposed faces. At the end of the watch, both pieces are lifted with separate hooks and placed on their own dry tiles. One has darkened at the edge; the other carries a similar mark near its cut. Talia refuses to call the result a corrosion ranking until the pair has been checked under a second set of conditions. The trial's value is that the pieces can be found and compared tomorrow, not that the first reading settles a workshop rule.

entries.title: A Matched Pair Does Not Describe a Basin
entries.body:
Both scraps were submerged in water collected at the upper channel on the same morning. One was wiped with a little Saltspool oil; the other was untreated. The treated scrap darkened less during this brief observation, though the cup had been stored under a cover before Rowan arrived. The test supports another matched trial. It does not report the channel's safety, a contamination source or change after rain. Talia leaves the cup's location and storage time visible, refusing to let an orderly table become a wider claim.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — keep the cup's storage place in the comparison

The covered cup sat on a shelf above the upper channel, away from direct spray. Talia adds a sketch of that shelf because a cup drawn simply as “channel water” could be mistaken for a sample taken from the flowing stream. Rowan repeats the test with a fresh cup and leaves it uncovered for the same interval before the scraps are placed inside. The treated and untreated pieces now show less contrast. Neither run is discarded: the storage difference may matter. A small trial records how its sample reached the bench, since the condition of a container can travel with the water it holds.

entries.title: Regional Fit Gauge: Build Record
entries.body:
The adjustable jaw gauge combines a steel blank, a reed packing strip and a little Saltspool oil on its hinge. The steel bears the force; the reed keeps grit away; the oil is used only on the hinge pin. Rowan forges one tool at Dawnkeep and stamps no single distance into its handle. Tomas asks him to scratch temporary marks during each field trial, then remove or relabel them when conditions change. The design carries a method for recording variation, not a final answer about every joint.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — tool custody is part of calibration

When the gauge leaves Dawnkeep Forge, Tomas ties its calibration card to the case with a loop that can be opened without cutting it. He writes the current jaw setting, the bench plate used for the check and the name of the forge keeping the tool overnight. At return, another smith can verify whether the jaws shifted in transit. Rowan asks if every borrower must sign. Tomas says the handoff can be marked by a workshop stamp instead, as long as the next custodian is clear. The gauge is shared property for this trial; its care should not depend on guessing who last carried it.

entries.title: The Gauge Found a Difference
entries.body:
At Gideon's stand the gauge holds against two clean surfaces of the hub, then slips across the old crack. That failure is useful: the instrument cannot measure a surface without a stable edge. Rowan leaves the mark beside the crack and writes 'do not infer fit across fracture.' The gauge does not decide whether the cart should carry a load. Gideon and Mira will test that question separately, with the axle pin installed and the cargo stated in advance.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — stop where the surface stops being stable

The jaw slides when it reaches the old crack, so Rowan paints a small boundary on the scrap board beside the hub rather than on Gideon's cart. Tomas examines the edge with a loupe and finds that the crack has lifted one side of the surface by a fraction. He refuses to force the gauge across it. The resulting reading would describe a tool slipping between two levels, not the fit of a replacement part. Gideon marks the cart for a separate repair inspection and keeps people clear of it until then. A measurement tool can reveal its own limit before it reveals a useful number.

entries.title: A Brace That Can Be Removed
entries.body:
Mara shows Rowan a living graft tied with bark fiber. It loosens after rain and tightens as it dries, helpful only because the tie is checked and replaced. A permanent metal clip holds the same branch differently. She will not call either method safer everywhere. The record must name plant, moisture and inspection interval, then explain how to remove the brace without tearing the stem. Rowan sketches the open side of the tie rather than a closed loop that could cut into new growth.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — let the person tending the branch choose the check

Mara shows Rowan where last season's tie began to rub after the rain softened its fibers. The mark is shallow, but she does not want the graft tightened by someone who has not watched it grow. She chooses the next inspection day with the gardener who waters that bed and asks that a second person be available to hold the branch, not pull it. Tomas adds both roles to the local note without assigning names to every future shift. A removable brace protects a plant only when it is tended with care. The person with daily knowledge of the stem must be able to ask for a different method.

entries.title: Glassplum Stem Notes
entries.body:
Mara's single bed has two stems that look alike at first glance. The one by the runoff line grew wider, though it also received water earlier in the rotation. Seed source, position and watering time are all recorded. Rowan cannot assign the difference to one factor from a single season. A stem can still serve as a fit sample when paired with a second piece cut at a known angle. Mara refuses to let the sample leave Greenwake without its label; an unlabeled piece would travel farther than its evidence.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — collect a cutting with the grower's label attached

Mara cuts one Glassplum stem below the last healthy joint and leaves its companion in the bed. She marks the sample with the seed packet, row and harvest date before it reaches Tomas's bench. A pollinator net had covered the bed for part of the morning, so the growing conditions were not identical to the open rows. Rowan includes that detail rather than calling the stem a typical Greenwake sample. Mara asks that the cut end be sealed before transport so it does not dry out and change shape. The cutting is material for a fit demonstration, not a token that transfers the garden's seed rights to the forge.

entries.title: An Adjustment with a Review Date
entries.body:
The tie supports the branch at two points and leaves a gap where the stem can thicken. Mara checks it at the next watering turn. A closed brace would be easier to draw, but its certainty could hide damage over time. Rowan records the fit as temporary and adds a review date rather than copying its width into a permanent template. The atlas needs an instruction for returning to a living object: the material may change after every measurement. The guide is not complete when a number is written; it is complete when someone knows when to measure again.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — a review date is not an expiry date

At the next watering turn, Mara checks whether the graft tie has begun to press into the stem. It has not, but one leaf has grown against the lower loop. She adjusts the tie by a finger's width and adds the change to the card. Tomas updates the diagram while keeping the first version visible. The review date prompted a look; it did not require the tie to be replaced automatically. Rowan asks whether the interval should be copied to the atlas. Mara says it belongs beside this plant's conditions, with a space for another gardener to choose a different interval after seeing the growth.

entries.title: Listening for a Shift, Not a Speaker
entries.body:
Lyra taps the test frame with a padded mallet, waits for the room to settle, then makes a second strike. The first sound overlaps a worker speaking outside; she discards that recording and retains only the marked interval after the doorway closes. Her log names the tool, frame and room, not the person whose voice crossed the sample. A longer ring may indicate looseness in this frame, but the room's stone and water also change resonance. Lyra records those conditions so future listeners can compare the setup without treating one pitch as a universal sign of failure.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — close the door without claiming the room is silent

Lyra shuts the Choir frame-room door after a worker leaves, then waits until the cart noise in the corridor passes. She hears water moving through the wall during the second ring and adds it to the log. The room is quieter, not silent. Rowan asks if she wants to keep the abandoned first recording. Lyra retains a note that it was discarded because it overlapped speech, but does not save the worker's voice or identify them. The atlas needs to say what condition changed between strikes. It does not need to turn an incidental speaker into part of a measurement they never agreed to join.

entries.title: Two Observations, Not One Cause
entries.body:
Rowan catches one Whisper Koi at the pool near the Choir frame. Its scales tremble briefly after the net is raised. Lyra's resonance test happened indoors before the catch, with a different tool and no shared recording. Both observations can stay in the atlas without being joined into a causal story. The entry names pool, date and handling, and notes that no population survey took place. A vivid detail makes a report easy to remember; it can also tempt a reader to supply a connection that the record does not contain.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — a vivid catch is still one catch

After Lyra finishes her frame test, Rowan returns to the pool and records the Whisper Koi catch separately. He notes that its scales trembled while the net was lifted, then stops handling it once the observation is complete. The resonance card carries a different time, room and instrument. Tomas considers adding a diagram that links the marks, but Lyra asks what experiment could disprove the connection first. They leave the pages adjacent in the binder without drawing an arrow between them. Readers may compare two records; the archive should not supply a cause merely because the same crew saw both events.

entries.title: Resonance Card with Its Room Attached
entries.body:
Lyra's card lists two strikes on one frame. The second began farther from the corner and produced a shorter ring. The interval can compare those trials, but the card also names room, water level and padded mallet. If any changes, the number may change. Lyra leaves a blank box for a new room instead of copying the first result everywhere. The field guide treats sound as a way to notice movement, not as a command that overrides a craftsperson's inspection.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — note the listener's position before the mallet falls

Lyra places a strip of blue tape where the observer stands and marks the frame's corner with a chalk dot. Rowan strikes from the opposite side on the next trial, keeping the mallet and force as close as he can. The ring seems shorter to him, although the card's timing differs by less than one beat. Lyra preserves the observer position as part of the setup. A later reader can repeat the frame test without treating a person's impression as an error. The instrument offers a comparison under stated conditions; it does not replace the craftsperson's hands, eyes or decision to inspect the joint.

entries.title: A Bracket Has a Weather Schedule
entries.body:
Ruth's crew checks the milepost bracket before storm season and after a visible swing. It is exposed to salt wind from the west; a sheltered inland bracket may not need the same schedule. Her predecessor copied a quarry's monthly check and found rust beneath the plate before the next inspection. The newer schedule is more frequent, but it is still local, not law. Rowan records wind direction, bracket material and the visible sign that triggers an extra check.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — the signal must remain readable during maintenance

Ruth refuses to take the milepost bracket down during the market day. Travelers rely on its arrow to find the dry road when the lower ford rises. Her crew puts a temporary marker on the opposite post and schedules the repair between wagon departures. Rowan records the temporary marker's position and when it will be removed. A maintenance plan that keeps a sign intact matters as much as the fastener schedule. The bracket's salt exposure still differs from an inland one, and the repair crew will review the schedule after winter. No one should mistake this local calendar for a universal interval.

entries.title: Wear Does Not Carry a Date
entries.body:
The lower fastener has a brighter scrape than the upper pair. Fine grit gathered beneath its plate, where each gust allowed a small movement. Ruth cannot say when it began; the bracket may have loosened over many storms or during one impact. Rowan photographs both fasteners before tightening the lower pin, preserving their difference without inventing a timeline. The marker remains legible during inspection. A maintenance note should explain how to check a joint without removing the signal travelers rely on.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — preserve the scrape before tightening the pin

Before Ruth turns the lower fastener, Rowan makes a rubbing of the bright scrape and photographs the grit beneath the plate. They save the rubbing with a note that the pin was loose at the time. After tightening, the bracket no longer rocks under a light hand. Ruth declines to call it repaired until a second crew checks it after the next strong wind. The before-image will help them see whether the movement returns. Tightening changed the evidence, so the record keeps both the original condition and the current one instead of overwriting the first with a neat final mark.

entries.title: Repeatability and the Hand Holding the Tool
entries.body:
Evelyn tests the gauge on a polished ring, then asks Rowan to repeat the fit without seeing her mark. The jaw returns to the same distance on the table, yet its angle differs between their hands. The tool may be sensitive to grip or to a small tilt in the surface. Evelyn refuses to average the numbers before they understand why. She records both operators and preserves the unadjusted scale. A repeated number is useful while the method still needs revision; removing the operator from the record would make disagreement impossible to reproduce.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — hide the first mark during the repeat

Evelyn covers her scale reading with a folded card before Rowan takes his turn with the gauge. He reads a slightly different angle and writes it down without seeing hers. They then exchange places and repeat once more. The second pair is closer, but not identical. Evelyn adds a note that the jaw may be held at a tilt and asks Tomas to make a guide for the operator's hand. She does not call one smith more accurate from two trials. Blinding the first mark reduces copying; it does not remove every difference in grip or judgment. The next change to the method remains visible in the record.

entries.title: Farwake Sample and Moving Water
entries.body:
The Farwake Carp was caught near the outer shelf after the current shifted twice. Rowan records depth and bait, then measures a loose scale beside the gauge. The fish is a local sample, not a representative of every body in the lake. Its scale bends under different pressure than brass or wood, so the readings are not directly comparable to the milepost bracket. Evelyn retains the catch because it shows where the instrument may need a softer jaw, not because it answers a question about the whole population.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — one scale can test softness, not identity

Tomas trims a small loose scale from the Farwake Carp sample only after Rowan records how it was caught and handled. The sample flexes beneath the gauge's brass jaw, so Evelyn inserts a padded contact and repeats the pressure test on a bench strip. The scale's response helps them decide whether a softer jaw is worth prototyping. It does not identify a sound at the lake or stand in for the fish itself. Rowan labels the scale as a detached sample and returns the remaining fish through the ordinary kitchen process. The atlas keeps craft use separate from claims about the lake's living population.

entries.title: A Difference Left in the Record
entries.body:
Evelyn's and Rowan's readings agree on the bench and differ at the outer pool rim. The first draft crossed out Rowan's result as an outlier. Evelyn restores it because the tool meets an uneven edge differently. Neither observation identifies the cause. The atlas records hand, angle and surface, then leaves room for a third trial. A guide preserving disagreement may look unfinished, but it gives another maker a path to test the instrument instead of inheriting false certainty.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — invite a third reader before choosing a number

Evelyn leaves the two disputed readings on the bench overnight and asks a smith from another shift to use the written setup without speaking to either of them first. The third reading falls between the two, but the observer notes that the outer rim is uneven. Tomas adds that condition to the margin and preserves all three values. The atlas does not gain certainty by voting among measurements. It gains another description of the surface and a reason to inspect the jaw design. Rowan keeps the word “outlier” crossed through but readable so the next editor can see how the first copy almost hid a real limitation.

entries.title: Copy Number Is Not an Owner
entries.body:
Nia numbers each copy by edition and date while leaving contributors' names optional. Corrections attach to a page so readers can compare versions without losing the earlier reading. Nia does not erase obsolete guidance; she marks when and why it was replaced. This preserves accountability without forcing a craftsperson to publish a personal history beside a practical tool. She adds a return slot for corrections and a printed note that using the gauge does not mean endorsing every later change.

Supplemental atlas workshop note —Supplemental atlas workshop note — ask before a name travels with a correction

A smith brings Nia a corrected measurement and asks to sign it with a workshop mark instead of a personal name. Nia explains that the mark will identify where the method was checked but may still let neighbors guess who wrote it. They choose an edition number and a return date, leaving the author line blank. The correction remains traceable through its source page and review process. Nia keeps the signed original in the restricted cabinet and sends an approved copy to the atlas. A useful correction does not require the writer to surrender more identity than the readers need to verify the method.

entries.title: The Atlas Decision
entries.body:
